# Preparations 

## Load packages

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| cache: false

library(tidyverse)
library(lavaan)
library(grateful)
library(knitr)
library(cowplot)
library(Hmisc)
library(corrplot)
library(purrr)
library(broom)
library(broom.mixed)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggh4x)
library(lmerTest)
```

Globals:
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| cache: false

avoi_short <- c("avoi_glo", "avoi_rom", "avoi_fri", "avoi_mot", "avoi_fat")
anxi_short <- c("anxi_glo", "anxi_rom", "anxi_fri", "anxi_mot", "anxi_fat")
outcomes_short <- c(avoi_short, anxi_short)

avoi_maj <- c("Avoidance: Global", "Avoidance: Romantic", "Avoidance: Best Friend", 
              "Avoidance: Mother", "Avoidance: Father")
anxi_maj <- c("Anxiety: Global", "Anxiety: Romantic", "Anxiety: Best Friend", 
              "Anxiety: Mother", "Anxiety: Father")
outcomes_maj <- c(avoi_maj, anxi_maj)

avoi_min <- c("avoidance (global)", "avoidance (romantic)", "avoidance (best friend)", 
              "avoidance (mother)", "avoidance (father)")
anxi_min <- c("anxiety (global)", "anxiety (romantic)", "anxiety (best friend)", 
              "anxiety (mother)", "anxiety (father)")
outcomes_min <- c(avoi_min, anxi_min)

outcomes <- tibble(short = outcomes_short,
                   maj = outcomes_maj,
                   min = outcomes_min)
```

# Load cleaned data

Cleaned, long file containing all waves of survey data from the CHILL study

```{r load}

base::load("data/cleaned/df_atta.rda")
base::load("data/cleaned/df_atta_rq1.rda")
```

## Last data preparation steps

Rename variables (attachment)
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false

df_atta <- df_atta %>% 
  rename(avoi_glo = avoide, avoi_rom = avoidc, avoi_fri = avoidd, avoi_mot = avoida, avoi_fat = avoidb,
         anxi_glo = anxietye, anxi_rom = anxietyc, anxi_fri = anxietyd, anxi_mot = anxietya, anxi_fat = anxietyb)

# in RQ1 df:
df_atta_rq1 <- df_atta_rq1 %>% 
  rename(avoi_glo_z = avoide_z, avoi_rom_z = avoidc_z, avoi_fri_z = avoidd_z, avoi_mot_z = avoida_z, avoi_fat_z = avoidb_z,
         anxi_glo_z = anxietye_z, anxi_rom_z = anxietyc_z, anxi_fri_z = anxietyd_z, anxi_mot_z = anxietya_z, anxi_fat_z = anxietyb_z)
```

Forgot to z-standardize age:
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false

# here, I'm using all persons' first obs for calculating M/SD
age_m <- df_atta %>% group_by(pid) %>% slice_head(n=1) %>% ungroup() %>% 
  summarise(age_m = mean(age_base, na.rm=T)) %>% pull(age_m)
age_sd <- df_atta %>% group_by(pid) %>% slice_head(n=1) %>% ungroup() %>% 
  summarise(age_sd = sd(age_base, na.rm=T)) %>% pull(age_sd)

df_atta <- df_atta %>% 
  mutate(age_base_z = ifelse(!is.na(age_base), (age_base - age_m) / age_sd, NA_real_))
```

Create wide format data for lavaan: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false

table(df_atta$time_month_rd)

df_atta_wide <- df_atta %>% 
  arrange(pid, time_month_rd) %>% 
  mutate(time_month_rd = sprintf("%02d", time_month_rd)) %>% # add zero padding
  select(-c(2:4, 23:32)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time_month_rd,
              names_sep = "_t",
              values_from = c(9:19))
# colnames(df_atta_wide)


# create factor designating the groups
df_atta_wide <- df_atta_wide %>% 
  mutate(grp = case_when(single_consist==1 ~ "Consistently single people",
                         partner_consist==1 ~ "Consistently partnered people",
                         partner_interm==1 ~ "Intermittently partnered people",
                         .default = NA_character_)) %>% 
  mutate(group_fct = factor(grp, 
                            levels = c("Consistently single people", "Consistently partnered people", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered people"), 
                            labels = c("Consistently single people", "Consistently partnered people", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered people"), ordered = TRUE)) %>%
  select(-grp)

table(df_atta_wide$group_fct) # looks good

# ... also add this to long df:
df_atta <- df_atta %>% 
  mutate(grp = case_when(single_consist==1 ~ "Consistently single people",
                         partner_consist==1 ~ "Consistently partnered people",
                         partner_interm==1 ~ "Intermittently partnered people",
                         .default = NA_character_)) %>% 
  mutate(group_fct = factor(grp, 
                            levels = c("Consistently single people", "Consistently partnered people", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered people"), 
                            labels = c("Consistently single people", "Consistently partnered people", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered people"), ordered = TRUE)) %>%
  select(-grp)

### create outcome-specific missingness indicators:
# if a person has missings in an outcome in *all* waves, they should be dropped later 
# in the respective analysis (not treated by FIML), which will be done through these indicators
outcome_vars_missi <- c(outcomes$short, "swb")

# we're doing this for the first 30 time points / months which matches 
# our later confirmatory
times_30 <- sprintf("%02d", 0:29)
# loop through all outcomes
for (outcome in outcome_vars_missi) {
  wave_vars <- paste0(outcome, "_t", times_30)
  df_atta_wide[[paste0(outcome, "_missi")]] <-
    as.integer(rowSums(is.na(df_atta_wide[, wave_vars])) == 30)
}
# I checked: these missingness indicators are relevant for friend- (n=1), mother- (n=374), and father-specific attachment (n=623) variables (same for avoidance and anxiety)

# no additional missings in life satisfaction
table(df_atta_wide$swb_missi, useNA = "always")
df_atta_wide <- df_atta_wide %>% select(-swb_missi) # dont need this

# for later robustness check, we're also doing a 24 months maximum
# -> I checked and these missingness indicators are exactly the same for 24 months (not needed)
```

Build group-specific data frames
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false

df_atta_wide_single_c <- df_atta_wide %>% 
  filter(single_consist==1) %>% 
  select(-c(single_consist, partner_consist, partner_interm))

df_atta_wide_partn_c <- df_atta_wide %>% 
  filter(partner_consist==1) %>% 
  select(-c(single_consist, partner_consist, partner_interm))

df_atta_wide_partn_i <- df_atta_wide %>% 
  filter(partner_interm==1) %>% 
  select(-c(single_consist, partner_consist, partner_interm))

# comparison of each partnered group with single
df_atta_wide_single_partn_c <- bind_rows(df_atta_wide_single_c, df_atta_wide_partn_c)
df_atta_wide_single_partn_i <- bind_rows(df_atta_wide_single_c, df_atta_wide_partn_i)
```

### Correlation matrices

Compute correlation matrices across time: I'm just using the first 3 months here as examples.  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"
#| cache: true

vars_m1 <- df_atta %>% 
  filter(time_month_rd==1) %>% 
  select(all_of(avoi_short), all_of(anxi_short), swb, single_consist, partner_consist, partner_interm)
cormat_m1 <- Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(vars_m1), type="pearson") # uses pairwise complete pairs
cormat_m1 <- cormat_m1$r

vars_m2 <- df_atta %>% 
  filter(time_month_rd==2) %>% 
  select(all_of(avoi_short), all_of(anxi_short), swb, single_consist, partner_consist, partner_interm)
cormat_m2 <- Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(vars_m2), type="pearson") # uses pairwise complete pairs
cormat_m2 <- cormat_m2$r

vars_m3 <- df_atta %>% 
  filter(time_month_rd==3) %>% 
  select(all_of(avoi_short), all_of(anxi_short), swb, single_consist, partner_consist, partner_interm)
cormat_m3 <- Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(vars_m3), type="pearson") # uses pairwise complete pairs
cormat_m3 <- cormat_m3$r

names_mat <- c(outcomes$maj, "Life Satisfaction", "Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered")

rownames(cormat_m1) <- names_mat
colnames(cormat_m1) <- names_mat
rownames(cormat_m2) <- names_mat
colnames(cormat_m2) <- names_mat
rownames(cormat_m3) <- names_mat
colnames(cormat_m3) <- names_mat
```

Plot: Correlation matrix at month 1
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 9

corrplot(cormat_m1, method="color", col=col(200),  
         type="lower", order="original", 
         addCoef.col = "black", # Add coefficient of correlation
         tl.col="black", tl.srt=15, #Text label color and rotation
```

### Variable distributions

#### Avoidance

Prepare df:
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

df_distr_plot_avoi_1_5 <- df_atta %>% 
  filter(time_month_rd %in% c(1:5)) %>% 
  rename(wave = time_month_rd) %>% 
  select(wave, all_of(avoi_short), swb) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(avoi_short, "swb"),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value") %>% 
  mutate(
    variable = factor(variable, levels = c(avoi_short, "swb"), labels = c(avoi_maj, "Life Satisfaction")), # relabel
    wave = factor(wave, levels = c(1:5), labels = paste0("M", c(1:5)))
```

### Plots: linear trends

Only focusing on the first 30 months for now to make this easier to read!  

Create df:  
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

attach_long <- df_atta %>%
  filter(time_month_rd <= 29) %>%
  select(pid, time_month_rd, all_of(avoi_short), all_of(anxi_short), group_fct) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(pid, time_month_rd, group_fct),
    names_to = c("type", "construct"),
    names_pattern = "(avoi|anxi)_(.*)",
    values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    construct = recode(construct,
                       glo = "Global",
                       rom = "Romantic",
                       fri = "Best Friend",
                       mot = "Mother",
                       fat = "Father"),
    construct = factor(construct,
                       levels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father")),
    type = recode(type,
                  avoi = "Avoidance",
                  anxi = "Anxiety"))

summary_attach <- attach_long %>%
  group_by(construct, type, time_month_rd) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(value))),
    n = sum(!is.na(value)),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_lower = mean_val - 1.96 * se,
         ci_upper = mean_val + 1.96 * se)

# by group:
summary_attach_group <- attach_long %>%
  group_by(construct, type, time_month_rd, group_fct) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(value))),
    n = sum(!is.na(value)),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_lower = mean_val - 1.96 * se,
         ci_upper = mean_val + 1.96 * se)
```

Show plot:

### Attrition analyses

#### Baseline predictors of study progress/completion

Reaching 12 / 24 months in the survey  

Create df:
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false

df_completion <- df_atta %>%
  group_by(pid) %>%
  summarise(last_month = max(time_month_rd, na.rm = TRUE),
            completed_12m = as.integer(last_month >= 12),
            completed_24m = as.integer(last_month >= 24))

table(df_completion$completed_12m)
prop.table(table(df_completion$completed_12m))

table(df_completion$completed_24m)
prop.table(table(df_completion$completed_24m))

# Merge with baseline variables
df_baseline <- df_atta %>%
  filter(time_month_rd == 0) %>%
  left_join(df_completion, by = "pid")
```

Run models (12 months):
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

preds <- c(
  "single_consist", "partner_consist", 
  "age_base", "man", 
  "avoi_glo", "avoi_mot", "avoi_fat", "avoi_rom", "avoi_fri",
  "anxi_glo", "anxi_mot", "anxi_fat", "anxi_rom", "anxi_fri",
  "swb"
)

# Fit all univariate models
uni_results_12 <- map_dfr(preds, function(x){

  fit <- glm(
    reformulate(x, response = "completed_12m"),
    family = binomial,
    data = df_baseline)

  tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(predictor = x)
})

# Fit the joint model
joint_fit_12 <- glm(
  reformulate(preds, response = "completed_12m"),
  family = binomial,
  data = df_baseline)

joint_results_12 <-
  tidy(joint_fit_12, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")
```

Show results (12 months):
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

results_12 <- uni_results_12 %>%
  select(predictor,
         uni_OR = estimate,
         uni_low = conf.low,
         uni_high = conf.high,
         uni_p = p.value) %>%
  left_join(
    joint_results_12 %>%
      select(term,
             joint_OR = estimate,
             joint_low = conf.low,
             joint_high = conf.high,
             joint_p = p.value),
    by = c("predictor" = "term"))

results_12 <- results_12 %>%
  mutate(
    `Univariate OR (95% CI)` =
      sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", uni_OR, uni_low, uni_high),

    `Joint OR (95% CI)` =
      sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", joint_OR, joint_low, joint_high),

    `Univariate p` = scales::pvalue(uni_p),
    `Joint p` = scales::pvalue(joint_p)) %>%
  select(
    Predictor = predictor,
    `Univariate OR (95% CI)`,
    `Univariate p`,
    `Joint OR (95% CI)`,
    `Joint p`)

knitr::kable(
  results_12,
  align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c"),
  caption = "Baseline predictors of completing the 12-month assessment."
)
```

# Confirmatory analyses

## RQ1: Prospective Selection Effects

From prereg: "In the sample of single people at baseline, we will run logistic regression models (with a logit link function) with consistent singlehood (0 = no, initially single but later find partner, 1 = yes, consistently single) as the outcome and both attachment anxiety and avoidance as predictors, which will be z-standardized. We will also include age and gender as control variables. Thus, we will run joint models for anxiety and avoidance but separate models for global attachment and each domain of attachment (i.e., in total 5 models with different attachment domains)."  

Logistic regression = pure between-person comparison  

### Global attachment

```{r selection-logistic-glo}
#| echo: true
#| cache: false
#| warning: false

formula_sel_glo <- as.formula(
  paste("single_consist", "~", paste(c("avoi_glo_z", "anxi_glo_z", "age_base", "man"), collapse = " + ")))

print(formula_sel_glo)

sel_glo <- glm(formula_sel_glo, 
                   family = binomial(link='logit'), data = df_atta_rq1)
summary(sel_glo)
```

```{r selection-logistic-rom}
sel_rom <- glm(formula_sel_rom,
```

### Results table

Gather estimates:
```{r selection-logistic-df}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

df_summa_sel_logist <- bind_rows(
  broom::tidy(sel_glo, conf.int = T, conf.level = .95, exponentiate = TRUE) %>% mutate(domain = "Global", n_obs = nobs(sel_glo)),
  broom::tidy(sel_rom, conf.int = T, conf.level = .95, exponentiate = TRUE) %>% mutate(domain = "Romantic", n_obs = nobs(sel_rom)),
  broom::tidy(sel_fri, conf.int = T, conf.level = .95, exponentiate = TRUE) %>% mutate(domain = "Best Friend", n_obs = nobs(sel_fri)),
  broom::tidy(sel_mot, conf.int = T, conf.level = .95, exponentiate = TRUE) %>% mutate(domain = "Mother", n_obs = nobs(sel_mot)),
  broom::tidy(sel_fat, conf.int = T, conf.level = .95, exponentiate = TRUE) %>% mutate(domain = "Father", , n_obs = nobs(sel_fat)))

df_summa_sel_logist <- df_summa_sel_logist %>% 
  mutate(domain_fct = factor(domain, 
                             levels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father"), 
                             labels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father"), ordered = TRUE))
```

```{r selection-logistic-table}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true

df_summa_sel_logist %>% 
  filter(term %in% c("avoi_glo_z", "anxi_glo_z",
                     "avoi_rom_z", "anxi_rom_z",
                     "avoi_fri_z", "anxi_fri_z",
                     "avoi_mot_z", "anxi_mot_z",
                     "avoi_fat_z", "anxi_fat_z")) %>%
  mutate(OR = estimate,
    CI_low = conf.low,
    CI_high = conf.high,
    pred = case_when(
      grepl("avoi", term) ~ "Avoidance",
      grepl("anxi", term) ~ "Anxiety"),
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", OR, CI_low, CI_high),
    p = format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)) %>%
  select(domain, pred, `OR (95% CI)`, p, n_obs) %>%
  arrange(factor(domain, levels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father")),
          pred) %>%
  kable()
```


::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Hypothesis confirmed for global and romantic avoidance, but n.s. for anxiety (which is also the case in single-predictor models): With higher global and romantic attachment avoidance, single people (at baseline) were more likely to remain single consistently throughout the observation period.  
In addition:  
- With higher friend-specific avoidance and anxiety, people were more likely to remain single.  
- With higher mother-specific anxiety, people were more likely to remain single (but n.s. for avoidance).  
:::

## RQ2: Changes in Attachment Models

From prereg: "To trace mean-level change in attachment across time, we will run univariate latent growth curve models based on manifest mean scale scores. We will start with separate models in each analysis group (consistently single, consistently partnered, intermittently partnered) and then extend those to multi-group models comparing consistently single people to each of the partnered groups."  

"The linear growth variable will be time at assessment (i.e., months centered at study entry). We run separate models for attachment anxiety and avoidance and for global attachment and each domain (2 x 5 attachment outcomes for each group comparison)."  

I'm doing the main models for all attachment domains in this section even though we only investigate global and romantic as confirmatory and the rest as exploratory. However, the entirely exploratory comparison of consistently single people and intermittently partnered individuals will follow below in the next section (5).  

### Example model

I'm first creating a template and show this with an example model of global avoidance (in singles, and then extended to single-partnered comparison). Below, I loop through all outcomes using the template.  

#### Single-group models

Specify model template, and show example model output:   

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true

# latent growth curve model: only 1 group
# Define number of assessment waves
n_waves <- 30  # t00 to t29

# Create variable names
times <- sprintf("%02d", 0:(n_waves - 1))
outcome_vars <- paste0("outcome_t", times)

# Intercept loadings
i_loadings <- paste0("1*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Slope loadings (scaled 0 to 1)
s_values <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_waves)
s_loadings <- paste0(round(s_values, 5), "*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Residual variance labels
residuals <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ res_", times, "*", outcome_vars, collapse = "\n")

# For plotting: Model-implied trajectory parameters (assuming age_base_z = 0, i.e., sample-average baseline age)
trajectory_estimates <- paste0("pred_t", times, " := a0 + a1*", round(s_values, 5), collapse = "\n")

# LGCM template
rq2_template <- paste0('
# Define intercept and slope factors
i =~ ', i_loadings, '

s =~ ', s_loadings, '

# Regress latent growth factors on baseline age
i ~ bi*age_base_z
s ~ bs*age_base_z

# Mean structure
i ~ a0*1
s ~ a1*1

# Variance structure
i ~~ vi*i
s ~~ vs*s
i ~~ cis*s

# Model-implied trajectories (for plotting)
', trajectory_estimates, '

# Residual variances
', residuals, '
')

# show the template:
cat(rq2_template)

# example model with global avoidance
model_rq2_avoi_glo_example <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template, "outcome", "avoi_glo")

# fit the models - 1 model for single, 1 for partnered
fit_rq2_avoi_glo_example <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_avoi_glo_example, data = df_atta_wide_single_c, 
                                           missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit_rq2_avoi_glo_example, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, ci = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
A few warning messages appear:  
- 1 case is dropped because of a missing value in age. This is no problem -> N = 592 now. (as an exogenous variable, missingsness in age is not handled with FIML)  
- Low coverage at later time points: this was to be expected, with increased dropout and up to 30 months of data (e.g., 84% missingness at t20, and 92% at t29). I think it's no big issue here, given that the model still converged, produced no implausible estimates, and resulted in decent fit indices (at least in the traditional ones; some of the "robust" ones could not be estimated properly...)  
- EM estimated variance-covariance matrix (Sigma) is (near) singular: also not surprising given the data structure and missingness -> lavInspect(fit_rq2_avoi_glo_example, "post.check") indicates TRUE, meaning that the final fitted model covariance structure is admissible  
- In pchisq(x2, df = df, ncp = ncp) : NaNs produced -> This may relate to some of the (robust) chi-square based fit statistics.  

--> Models were estimated using FIML to account for missing observations. Due to the longitudinal design and increasing attrition at later waves, some covariance estimates were based on limited pairwise coverage. All models converged and yielded admissible solutions.  
--> Below, we provide more details on all models in "Model fit" and "Model diagnostics".  
:::

Now show results for partnered: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true

fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_c_example <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_avoi_glo_example, data = df_atta_wide_partn_c, 
                                           missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_c_example, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, ci = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Quick summary of main results:  

Global avoidance decreases over time in both groups, with slightly more pronounced decreases in single people. No significant age moderation (but good that we control for age differences).  

No strong support for our hypothesis of differential change (on the descriptive level) - next, we test these slope differences formally in a multi-group model.  
:::

#### Multi-group model

Extend to multi-group model to compare single ("_s") vs. partnered people ("_p")  

Freely estimated group differences by default; group-specific age effects; group-specific intercept/slope means; group-specific variances; group-specific residual variances; same time metric across groups (0 -> 1 scaling over 29 months)  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true

# latent growth curve model: multi-group
# ... I dont repeat the parts here that stay the same: n_waves, times, outcome_vars, etc.

# Residual variance labels (group-specific)
residuals_multi <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ c(\"r", times, "_s\", \"r", times, "_p\")*", outcome_vars, collapse = "\n")

# For plotting: Model-implied trajectory parameters (assuming age_base_z = 0, i.e., sample-average baseline age)
trajectory_estimates_multi <- paste0("pred_t", times, "_s := a0_s + a1_s*", round(s_values, 5),
                                     "\n",
                                     "pred_t", times, "_p := a0_p + a1_p*", round(s_values, 5), collapse = "\n")

# Multi-group LGCM template
rq2_template_multi <- paste0('
# Define intercept and slope factors
i =~ ', i_loadings, '

s =~ ', s_loadings, '

# Regress latent growth factors on baseline age
i ~ c("bi_s", "bi_p")*age_base_z
s ~ c("bs_s", "bs_p")*age_base_z

# Mean structure
i ~ c("a0_s", "a0_p")*1
s ~ c("a1_s", "a1_p")*1

# Variance structure
i ~~ c("vi_s", "vi_p")*i
s ~~ c("vs_s", "vs_p")*s
i ~~ c("cis_s", "cis_p")*s

# Model-implied trajectories (for plotting)
', trajectory_estimates_multi, '

# Residual variances
', residuals_multi, '

')

# show the template:
cat(rq2_template_multi)

# Example model with global avoidance
model_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_example <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi, "outcome", "avoi_glo")

# Fit model
fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_example <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_example,
                                      data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_c %>% arrange(group_fct),
                                      group = "group_fct",
                                      missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Similar warning messages as above. See my explanation there.  
:::

Show results: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true

summary(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_example, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, ci = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Descriptively, the global avoidance decreases are somewhat more pronounced in single people compared to partnered people. Single people also start with higher avoidance at baseline. The difference in slopes is not sufficient, though, to "offset" this initial intercept difference. No significant age moderation in either group.  
:::

Formal test of group differences: Likelihood ratio tests to assess whether constraining the latent slope parameters to be equal across groups significantly worsens model fit relative to a model with freely estimated slopes.  

(same warning messages here as above - I suppress them here)
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: true

# latent growth curve model: multi-group 
# -> create an intermediate model where the latent slope parameter is constrained to be equal across groups

rq2_template_multi_constr <- stringr::str_replace(rq2_template_multi, 
                                                  's ~ c\\("a1_s", "a1_p"\\)\\*1', 's ~ a1*1')
rq2_template_multi_constr <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr, 'a1_s', 'a1')
rq2_template_multi_constr <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr, 'a1_p', 'a1')

model_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_constr <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr, "outcome", "avoi_glo")

fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_constr <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_constr,
                                                  data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_c %>% arrange(group_fct),
                                                  group = "group_fct",
                                                  missing = "fiml",
                                                  verbose = FALSE)
```

LRT: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true

anova(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_example, fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_constr)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
No significant group differences in the slopes according to LRT: Constraining the latent slopes to be equal across groups did not significantly worsen model fit, providing no evidence that the groups differed in their rates of attachment change.
:::

### Template loop & extraction

Run loop over all 5 X 2 outcomes  

(Here in the loop I suppress lavaan warnings in the html output, but they are pretty much the same ones as shown above for the example model. In the sections below, I go into model fit and diagnostics more systematically.)  

```{r rq2-loop}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_models) { # we can toggle this on/off in the YAML heading
  
# loop across all attachment outcomes
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
#for (i in 1:2) {
  print(paste0("Running outcome: ", outcomes$maj[i]))
  
  # Outcome-specific missingness indicator -> added this mostly for parent-specific attachment
  missi_var <- paste0(outcomes$short[i], "_missi")
  
  # Step 1: fill single-group model template (2x, 1 for single, 1 for partnered)
  print("-> Step 1")
  model_rq2 <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2 <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2,
                            data = df_atta_wide_single_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                            missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i])), fit_rq2))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], ".rds"))
  
  fit_rq2_partn_c <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2,
                            data = df_atta_wide_partn_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                            missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_c")), fit_rq2_partn_c))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_partn_c, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_c.rds"))

  # Step 2: fill free multigroup model template
  print("-> Step 2")
  model_rq2_multi <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_multi <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_multi,
                                  data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_c  %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0) %>%
                                    arrange(group_fct),
                                  group = "group_fct",
                                  missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i])), fit_rq2_multi))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_multi, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], ".rds"))

  # Step 3: fill constrained multigroup model template
  print("-> Step 3")
  model_rq2_multi_constr <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_multi_constr <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_multi_constr,
                                         data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_c  %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0) %>%
                                           arrange(group_fct),
                                         group = "group_fct",
                                         missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_constr")), fit_rq2_multi_constr))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_multi_constr, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_constr.rds"))

  # Step 4: likelihood ratio test: free vs constrained slopes
  print("-> Step 4")
  lrt <- anova(fit_rq2_multi, fit_rq2_multi_constr)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("lrt_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i])), lrt))
  saveRDS(lrt, file = paste0("models/lrt_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], ".rds"))
}
}
```

```{r rq2-load-extract}
    assign(paste0("lrt_rq2_mg_", x), readRDS(paste0("models/lrt_rq2_mg_", x, ".rds")))
  }
}

### single-group lavaan models:
# custom function for parameter extraction
extract_lav_rq2 <- function(fit_obj) {
  name_obj <- as.character(substitute(fit_obj))
  name_outc <- name_obj %>% 
    str_remove("fit_rq2_") %>% 
    str_remove("_partn_c$")
  group_lab <- ifelse(str_detect(name_obj, "partn_c$"),
                      "Consistently partnered",
                      "Consistently single")
  # use tidy() for extraction
  broom::tidy(fit_obj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("a0", "a1", "cis", "bi", "bs", "vi", "vs")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           group_fct = factor(group_lab, 
                            levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered"), 
                            labels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
    select(outc, group_fct, term = label, est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
           z_value = statistic, p_value = p.value, est_std = std.all)
}

# bind all model outputs together
rq2_summary_single <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_glo),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_rom),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_fri),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_mot),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_fat),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_glo),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_rom),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_fri),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_mot),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_fat),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_rom_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_fri_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_mot_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_avoi_fat_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_glo_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_rom_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_fri_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_mot_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq2(fit_rq2_anxi_fat_partn_c)
)

# Add labels
rq2_summary_single <- rq2_summary_single %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))#

### multi-group lavaan models
# custom function for parameter extraction 
extract_lav_rq2_mg <- function(fit_obj, lrt_obj) {
  name_obj <- as.character(substitute(fit_obj))
  name_outc <- str_remove(name_obj, "fit_rq2_mg_")
  
  # extract LRT information
  lrt_tab <- as.data.frame(lrt_obj)
  lrt_chi <- lrt_tab$`Chisq diff`[2]
  lrt_df <- lrt_tab$`Df diff`[2]
  lrt_p <- lrt_tab$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
  
  # extract model parameters
  broom::tidy(fit_obj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("a0_s", "a0_p", "a1_s", "a1_p", "cis_s", "cis_p",
                        "bi_s", "bi_p", "bs_s", "bs_p", "vi_s", "vi_p", "vs_s", "vs_p")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           group_fct = case_when(str_detect(label, "_s$") ~ "Consistently single",
                                 str_detect(label, "_p$") ~ "Consistently partnered",
                                 TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      group_fct = factor(group_fct, levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered",
                                    "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE),
      lrt_chi = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_chi, NA),
      lrt_df = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_df, NA),
      lrt_p = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_p, NA)) %>% 
    select(outc, group_fct, term = label,
           est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
           z_value = statistic, p_value = p.value, est_std = std.all,
           lrt_chi, lrt_df, lrt_p)
}

# bind all model outputs together
rq2_summary_mg <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_glo),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_rom, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_rom),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fri, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_fri),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_mot, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_mot),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fat, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_fat),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_glo, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_glo),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_rom, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_rom),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fri, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_fri),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_mot, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_mot),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fat, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_fat)
)

# Add labels
rq2_summary_mg <- rq2_summary_mg %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))
```

### Model fit

Fit statistics: single-group models  
-> These fit indices are very computationally expensive. I put them in a conditional chunk and load them as an RDS object in the next chunk.  

```{r calc-fit-rq2}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_expensive) { # only run when we allow this in YAML heading
  
# model fit statistics: single-group models
rq2_fit_single <- outcomes$short %>% 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(x) {
    bind_rows(
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq2_", x))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Consistently single"),
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq2_", x, "_partn_c"))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Consistently partnered"))
  }) %>% 
  select(outc, group_fct, nobs, npar, AIC, BIC, cfi, rmsea, srmr) %>% 
  mutate(
    outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
    group_fct = factor(group_fct,
                       levels = c("Consistently single",
                                  "Consistently partnered",
                                  "Intermittently partnered"),
                       ordered = TRUE))

# save externally:
saveRDS(rq2_fit_single, "model_fit/rq2_fit_single.rds")
}
```

### Model diagnostics

- Did the model converge?  
- Did lavaan's internal check pass?  
- Are there inadmissible negative variances?  

#### Single-group models

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# diagnostics for all single-group and partnered RQ2 models
rq2_models <- c("fit_rq2_avoi_glo", "fit_rq2_avoi_rom",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fri", "fit_rq2_avoi_mot",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fat", "fit_rq2_anxi_glo",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_rom", "fit_rq2_anxi_fri",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_mot", "fit_rq2_anxi_fat",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_c", "fit_rq2_avoi_rom_partn_c",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fri_partn_c", "fit_rq2_avoi_mot_partn_c",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fat_partn_c", "fit_rq2_anxi_glo_partn_c",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_rom_partn_c", "fit_rq2_anxi_fri_partn_c",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_mot_partn_c", "fit_rq2_anxi_fat_partn_c")

rq2_diagnostics <- purrr::map_dfr(rq2_models, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(parameterEstimates(fit)$op == "~~" &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$lhs == parameterEstimates(fit)$rhs &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$est < 0))
})

rq2_diagnostics %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
These diagnostics all look good.  
:::

#### Multi-group models

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq2_mg_models <- c("fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo", "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_rom",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fri", "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_mot",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fat", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_glo",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_rom", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fri",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_mot", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fat")

rq2_mg_diagnostics <- purrr::map_dfr(rq2_mg_models, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(pe$op == "~~" &
                          pe$lhs == pe$rhs &
                          pe$est < 0))
})

rq2_mg_diagnostics %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

### Summary plot

Create plots for manuscript: start with extracting the parameters

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Custom function to extract model-implied trajectories from lavaan defined parameters
extract_rq2_plot_traject <- function(fit, outcome_label) {
  parameterEstimates(fit, ci = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(op == ":=") %>%
    mutate(group = case_when(str_detect(lhs, "_s$") ~ "Consistently single",
                             str_detect(lhs, "_p$") ~ "Consistently partnered"),
           month = as.numeric(str_extract(lhs, "(?<=t)\\d+")),
           time_years = month / 12,
           outcome = outcome_label) %>%
    select(outcome, group, month, time_years, estimate = est, ci_low = ci.lower, ci_high = ci.upper)
}

# Extract trajectories from all multi-group RQ2 models
plot_traject_list_rq2 <- list()
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
  fit <- readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], ".rds"))
  plot_traject_list_rq2[[i]] <- extract_rq2_plot_traject(fit, outcomes$maj[i])
}
plot_traject_df_rq2 <- bind_rows(plot_traject_list_rq2)

# Check extracted plotting dataframe
head(plot_traject_df_rq2)
table(plot_traject_df_rq2$outcome, plot_traject_df_rq2$group)

# create factor variables:
plot_traject_df_rq2 <- plot_traject_df_rq2 %>%
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes$maj, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
         group_fct = factor(group, levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered"), ordered = TRUE))

# a bit tricky: handling variable y-axis ranges...
# Define common y-axis width across facets
y_range_rq2 <- 1.7
# Calculate facet-specific y-axis limits with equal zoom
plot_traject_limits_rq2 <- plot_traject_df_rq2 %>%
  group_by(outc_fct) %>%
  summarise(y_mid = mean(range(c(ci_low, ci_high)))) %>%
  mutate(y_lower = y_mid - y_range_rq2 / 2,
         y_upper = y_mid + y_range_rq2 / 2)
# Create facet-specific y-axis scales with half-point breaks
y_scales_rq2 <- lapply(1:nrow(plot_traject_limits_rq2), function(i) {
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(plot_traject_limits_rq2$y_lower[i],
                                plot_traject_limits_rq2$y_upper[i]),
                     breaks = seq(floor(plot_traject_limits_rq2$y_lower[i] * 2) / 2,
                                  ceiling(plot_traject_limits_rq2$y_upper[i] * 2) / 2,
                                  by = 0.5),
                     labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1))
})

# Create significance labels from LRT p-values
rq2_sig_labels <- rq2_table_mg_a %>%
  filter(term == "a1_s") %>%
  mutate(sig = case_when(lrt_p < .001 ~ "***",
                         lrt_p < .01 ~ "**",
                         lrt_p < .05 ~ "*",
                         TRUE ~ "")) %>%
  select(outc_fct, sig) %>% 
  mutate(outc_label = ifelse(sig == "", as.character(outc_fct), paste0(as.character(outc_fct), " (", sig, ")")))
# Add labelled outcome factor for plotting
plot_traject_df_rq2 <- plot_traject_df_rq2 %>%
  left_join(rq2_sig_labels %>% select(outc_fct, outc_label), by = "outc_fct") %>%
  mutate(outc_fct_label = factor(outc_label, levels = unique(outc_label))) %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct_label = factor(outc_fct_label, levels = unique(outc_fct_label), ordered = TRUE))
```

Create and save plot: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Define custom group colours and linetypes
group_colors <- c("Consistently single" = "#008837", "Consistently partnered" = "#A23E48")
group_linetypes <- c("Consistently single" = "solid", "Consistently partnered" = "longdash")

# Plot RQ2 model-implied trajectories with 95% confidence bands
plot_rq2_traject <- ggplot(plot_traject_df_rq2, aes(x = time_years, y = estimate, 
                                                     colour = group_fct, fill = group_fct,
                                                     linetype = group_fct)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), alpha = .20, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = group_linetypes) +
  facet_wrap(~outc_fct_label, ncol = 2, nrow = 5, scales = "free_y", dir = "v") +
  ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales(y = y_scales_rq2) +
  labs(x = "Years since baseline", y = "Attachment domain (model-implied; 95% CI-band)", 
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         fill = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         linetype = guide_legend(title = "Group")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())

# save as pdf
pdf(width = 6.5, height = 7.5, "figures/rq2_traject.pdf")
plot_rq2_traject
dev.off()
```

Show plot: 
```{r rq2-summary-plot-show}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 9.5
#| cache: false

plot_rq2_traject
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
No support for our hypotheses and overall only very limited evidence that consistently single vs. partnered people change differently in their attachment over time. Some of the gaps are still quite sizeable, reflecting baseline differences and potentially selection effects - especially for global avoidance and anxiety as well as romantic avoidance and anxiety. Also, somewhat of a gap in friend-specific anxiety. Single people are less securely attached in these domains throughout.
:::

## RQ3: Co-Development of Attachment and Life Satisfaction

From prereg: "To examine co-development, we will estimate bivariate latent growth curve models of attachment and life satisfaction within the group of consistently single people, as well as exploratorily in the each of the partnered groups. These will build progressively on the univariate models (RQ2), adding life satisfaction as the second construct."  

"The main effects of interest are the cross-construct intercept-slope correlations and slope-slope correlations. Again, we will run separate models for the different attachment variables (2 x 5 models in each group)."  

I'm doing the main models for all attachment domains in this section (in single people), even though we only investigate global and friend-specific as confirmatory and the rest as exploratory. However, the exploration of consistently partnered people and intermittently partnered individuals will follow below in the next section.  

### Example model

I'm first creating a template and show this with an example model of global avoidance (in single people). Below, I loop through all outcomes using the template.  

Specify model template, and show example model output:   

(Terminology: "a" is for attachment in the RQ3 code, and "w" for well-being = life satisfaction)  
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true

# bivariate latent growth curve model: single-group

# Define number of assessment waves
n_waves <- 30  # t00 to t29

# Create variable names
times <- sprintf("%02d", 0:(n_waves - 1))
outcome_vars <- paste0("outcome_t", times)
swb_vars <- paste0("swb_t", times)

# Intercept loadings
i_loadings_out <- paste0("1*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")
i_loadings_swb <- paste0("1*", swb_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Slope loadings (scaled 0 to 1)
s_values <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_waves)
s_loadings_out <- paste0(round(s_values, 5), "*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")
s_loadings_swb <- paste0(round(s_values, 5), "*", swb_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Residual variance labels
res_out <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ ra", times, "*", outcome_vars, collapse = "\n")
res_swb <- paste0(swb_vars, " ~~ rw", times, "*", swb_vars, collapse = "\n")

# Residual covariance labels
res_cov <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ rc", times, "*", swb_vars, collapse = "\n")

# Bivariate LGCM template
rq3_template <- paste0('
# Define intercept and slope factors
ia =~ ', i_loadings_out, '
sa =~ ', s_loadings_out, '

iw =~ ', i_loadings_swb, '
sw =~ ', s_loadings_swb, '

# Regress latent growth factors on baseline age
ia ~ bia*age_base_z
sa ~ bsa*age_base_z
iw ~ biw*age_base_z
sw ~ bsw*age_base_z

# Mean structure
ia ~ a0*1
sa ~ a1*1
iw ~ w0*1
sw ~ w1*1

# Variance structure
ia ~~ via*ia
sa ~~ vsa*sa
ia ~~ cisa*sa

iw ~~ viw*iw
sw ~~ vsw*sw
iw ~~ cisw*sw

# Cross-process covariances
ia ~~ cii*iw
ia ~~ cis_aw*sw
iw ~~ cis_wa*sa
sa ~~ css*sw

# Residual variances
', res_out, '

', res_swb, '

# Residual covariances
', res_cov, '
')

# Example model with global avoidance
model_rq3_avoi_glo_example <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq3_template, "outcome", "avoi_glo")

# Fit model
fit_rq3_avoi_glo_example <- lavaan::growth(model_rq3_avoi_glo_example,
                                           data = df_atta_wide_single_c,
                                           missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Same types of warning messages here as for RQ2 models. See model fit and model diagnostics sections below.
:::

Show results: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true

summary(fit_rq3_avoi_glo_example, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, ci = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Global avoidance decreases and life satisfaction increases. Significant (negative) co-development.    

I also tried out an otherwise identical model without residual covariances but fit was worse, supporting the retention of the residual covariance structure. These residual covariances also make sense from a theoretical standpoint because they account for occasion-specific shared influences not captured by the latent trajectories.    
:::

### Template loop & extraction

Run loop over all 5 X 2 outcomes  

(Here in the loop, I suppress lavaan warnings in the html output, but they are very similar to the ones shown above for the example model. Below, I go into model diagnostics more systematically.)   

```{r rq3-loop}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_models) {
  
# loop across all attachment outcomes
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) { # we can toggle this on/off in the YAML heading
  print(paste0("Running outcome: ", outcomes$maj[i]))

  # Fill bivariate LGCM template
  model_rq3 <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq3_template, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  
  # Outcome-specific missingness indicator -> added this mostly for parent-specific attachment
  missi_var <- paste0(outcomes$short[i], "_missi")

  # Fit model in consistently single people
  fit_rq3 <- lavaan::growth(model_rq3,
                            data = df_atta_wide_single_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                            missing = "fiml",
                            verbose = FALSE)

  # Save model object
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i])), fit_rq3))
  saveRDS(fit_rq3, file = paste0("models/fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i], ".rds"))
}
}
```

Create summary table of all effects of interest: parameter extraction  
(... based on broom::tidy() giving unstandardized effects & SE / CI)  
```{r rq3-load-extract}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Load saved models when run_models = FALSE
if (!params$run_models) {
  for (x in outcomes$short) {
    assign(paste0("fit_rq3_", x), readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq3_", x, ".rds")))
  }
}

# custom function for parameter extraction from bivariate LGCMs
extract_lav_rq3 <- function(fit_obj) {
  name_obj <- as.character(substitute(fit_obj))
  name_outc <- name_obj %>% 
    str_remove("fit_rq3_") %>% 
    str_remove("_partn_c$|_partn_i$")
  group_lab <- case_when(str_detect(name_obj, "_partn_c$") ~ "Consistently partnered",
                         str_detect(name_obj, "_partn_i$") ~ "Intermittently partnered",
                         TRUE ~ "Consistently single")
  # filter parameters of interest
  broom::tidy(fit_obj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("a0", "a1", "w0", "w1",
                        "bia", "bsa", "biw", "bsw",
                        "via", "vsa", "cisa",
                        "viw", "vsw", "cisw",
                        "cii", "cis_aw", "cis_wa", "css")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           group_fct = factor(group_lab, levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered",
                                                    "Intermittently partnered"),
                              ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
    select(outc, group_fct, term = label,
           est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
           z_value = statistic, p_value = p.value,
           est_std = std.all)
}

# bind all model outputs together
rq3_summary <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_glo),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_rom),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fri),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_mot),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fat),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_glo),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_rom),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fri),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_mot),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fat)
)
# Add labels
rq3_summary <- rq3_summary %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short,
                           labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))
```

For the preregistered effects of interest, I use lavaan::standardizedSolution(). For the cross-construct latent growth-factor covariances, standardization yields correlations rather than covariances. The standardized estimates have their own SEs, CIs, and p-values, which can differ slightly from those of the corresponding unstandardized covariances. This matches the preregistration: “The main effects of interest are the cross-construct intercept-slope correlations and slope-slope correlations.”  

The standardized effect size is always the same as the est_std / std.all one from broom::tidy(), though.  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Extract standardized slope-slope correlation and CI
extract_rq3_cross_std <- function(fit_obj, name_obj) {
  name_outc <- name_obj %>% 
    stringr::str_remove("fit_rq3_") %>% 
    stringr::str_remove("_partn_c$|_partn_i$")
  
  lavaan::standardizedSolution(fit_obj, ci = TRUE) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("cii", "cis_aw", "cis_wa", "css")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           est = est.std,
           ci_lo = ci.lower,
           ci_hi = ci.upper) %>% 
    select(outc, term = label, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value = pvalue)
}

# Extract all RQ3 slope-slope correlations
rq3_models <- c("fit_rq3_avoi_glo", "fit_rq3_avoi_rom",
                "fit_rq3_avoi_fri", "fit_rq3_avoi_mot",
                "fit_rq3_avoi_fat", "fit_rq3_anxi_glo",
                "fit_rq3_anxi_rom", "fit_rq3_anxi_fri",
                "fit_rq3_anxi_mot", "fit_rq3_anxi_fat")

rq3_extracted_cross <- bind_rows(lapply(rq3_models, function(x) {
  extract_rq3_cross_std(get(x), x)
})) %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(domain_fct = factor(str_remove(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety): "), 
                             levels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father"),
                             ordered = TRUE),
         pred_fct = factor(str_extract(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety)"), 
                           levels = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety"),
                           ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, term) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, domain_fct, pred_fct)
```

### Model fit

Fit statistics: single-group models  
-> These fit indices are very computationally expensive. I put them in a conditional chunk and load them as an RDS object in the next chunk.  

```{r calc-fit-rq3}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_expensive) { # only run when we allow this in YAML heading

# model fit statistics: single-group models
rq3_fit_single <- outcomes$short %>% 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(x) {
    bind_rows(
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq3_", x))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Consistently single"))
  }) %>% 
  select(outc, group_fct, nobs, npar, AIC, BIC, cfi, rmsea, srmr) %>% 
  mutate(
    outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
    group_fct = factor(group_fct,
                       levels = c("Consistently single",
                                  "Consistently partnered",
                                  "Intermittently partnered"),
                       ordered = TRUE))

# save externally:
saveRDS(rq3_fit_single, "model_fit/rq3_fit_single.rds")
}
```

Show fit indices table: 
```{r show-fit-rq3}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false

rq3_fit_single <- readRDS("model_fit/rq3_fit_single.rds")

rq3_fit_single %>% select(-outc) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, everything()) %>% 
  kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
RMSEA looks good but CFI and SRMR are below conventional thresholds. Important to keep in mind that these models were specified primarily to model longitudinal change and covariation among manifest variables, rather than to establish a latent measurement model.  

Fit is pretty similar across outcomes, with the exception of Avoidance: Best Friend. Here, the latent slope variance is considerably larger than in the global model. This means friend-avoidance has much more heterogeneous trajectories and a single linear slope will fit relatively poorly. Other than that, there is no indication for "technical" issues with this model or implausible estimates. Occasion-specific variation (in the residuals) is also quite large here. Another explanation could be nonlinear change. However, in the observed means, a linear slope looks like a reasonable approximation of the trajectory (descriptively).   
:::

### Model diagnostics

- Did the model converge?  
- Did lavaan's internal check pass?  
- Are there inadmissible negative variances?  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# diagnostics for all single-group and partnered RQ2 models
rq3_diagnostics <- purrr::map_dfr(rq3_models, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(parameterEstimates(fit)$op == "~~" &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$lhs == parameterEstimates(fit)$rhs &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$est < 0))
})

rq3_diagnostics %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Again, no issues here.   
:::

### Summary tables

Latent intercept and slope factors: "alpha0" (a0 = attach, w0 = life sat) & "alpha1" (a1 = attach, w1 = life sat): 

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_a <- rq3_summary %>% 
  filter(term=="a0" | term=="a1" | term=="w0" | term=="w1") %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, group_fct, term) %>% 
  mutate(sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, sig, est_std)

rq3_table_a %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 4, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_a))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Life satisfaction increases that are very similar across models (roughly *d* = .31 when standardized; a bit larger in the mother/father models). The attachment changes match the estimates from the univariate models relatively closely (and are all significant).  
:::

Latent intercept / slope variances & covariance - general terminology:  
- (a) = attachment  
- (w) = well-being (life satisf.)  
- (c) = covariance (or: correlation in the standardized solution)    
- (v) = variance  
- (i) = latent intercept  
- (s) = latent slope   

Cross-construct correlations based on the standardized solutions:  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_cross <- rq3_extracted_cross %>% 
  filter(term %in% c("cii", "cis_aw", "cis_wa", "css")) %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, term) %>% 
  mutate(group = "Consistently single", 
         sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, sig)

rq3_table_cross %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 4, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_cross))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
The intercept-intercept correlations are all negative and significant (*p* < .001): With higher attachment insecurity (both avoidance and anxiety), people have lower life satisfaction.  

The intercept-slope correlations are a bit more varied but mostly not significant. Exceptions are that:  
- Single people with higher initial life satisfaction decreased (even) more in global attachment avoidance.  
- Single people with higher initial life satisfaction increased more in mother-specific attachment anxiety (or decreased less).  
- Single people with higher initial father-specific attachment anxiety, increased more in life satisfaction.  

For slope-slope correlations, see below!  
:::

Focus on parameter that is relevant to hypothesis: slope-slope correlation (standardized solution)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_cross %>% 
  filter(term=="css") %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Slope-slope correlations indicate negative co-development of attachement insecurity and life satisfaction that is significant for all domains, except for friend-specific attachment avoidance (*r* = -0.045). Otherwise, correlations range from *r* = -0.188 (romantic attachment avoidance) to *r* = -0.393 (global attachment avoidance).  

This supports our hypothesis for global and romantic attachment. (Rest of the domains were exploratory)  
:::

Within-construct intercept-slope covariances:

Only some of the attachment intercept-slope covariances are significant, but none for life satisfaction. Not super important für our RQs but it generally seems that people who start out higher in attachment insecurity then decrease more over time.

### Summary plot

We're plotting the standardized effects (i.e., slope-slope correlations). See prereg: "The main effects of interest are the cross-construct intercept-slope correlations and slope-slope correlations."

# Exploratory analyses

## RQ2: Changes in Attachment Models (intermittently partnered)

From prereg: "For all attachment models, we will also explore whether consistently single people experience differential changes in attachment compared to intermittently partnered individuals."  

We don't need to adjust the template. Same as above, we just use different groups.

### Template loop & extraction

Run loop over all 5 X 2 outcomes  

```{r rq2-loop-expl}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# make factor ordering explicit again:
df_atta_wide_single_partn_i <- df_atta_wide_single_partn_i %>% 
  mutate(group_fct = factor(group_fct, levels = c("Consistently single people", 
                                                  "Intermittently partnered people"), 
                            labels = c("Consistently single", "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE))

levels(df_atta_wide_single_partn_i$group_fct)

if (params$run_models) { # we can toggle this on/off in the YAML heading
  
# loop across all attachment outcomes
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
#for (i in 1:2) {
  print(paste0("Running outcome: ", outcomes$maj[i]))
  
  # Outcome-specific missingness indicator -> added this mostly for parent-specific attachment
  missi_var <- paste0(outcomes$short[i], "_missi")
  
  # Step 1: fill single-group model template for intermittently partnered people
  print("-> Step 1")
  model_rq2 <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_partn_i <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2,
                                     data = df_atta_wide_partn_i %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                                     missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_i")), fit_rq2_partn_i))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_partn_i, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_i.rds"))
  
  # Step 2: fill free multigroup model template
  print("-> Step 2")
  model_rq2_multi <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_multi_si <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_multi,
                                     data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_i %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0) %>%
                                       arrange(group_fct),
                                     group = "group_fct",
                                     missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_si")), fit_rq2_multi_si))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_multi_si, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_si.rds"))
  
  # Step 3: fill constrained multigroup model template
  print("-> Step 3")
  model_rq2_multi_constr <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_multi_si_constr <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_multi_constr,
                                            data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_i %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0) %>%
                                              arrange(group_fct),
                                            group = "group_fct",
                                            missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_si_constr")), fit_rq2_multi_si_constr))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_multi_si_constr, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_si_constr.rds"))
  
  # Step 4: likelihood ratio test: free vs constrained slopes
  print("-> Step 4")
  lrt_si <- anova(fit_rq2_multi_si, fit_rq2_multi_si_constr)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("lrt_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_si")), lrt_si))
  saveRDS(lrt_si, file = paste0("models/lrt_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_si.rds"))
}
}
```
Create summary table of all effects of interest:  

First, parameter extraction  
```{r rq2-load-extract-expl}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Load saved models when run_models = FALSE
if (!params$run_models) {
  for (x in outcomes$short) {
    assign(paste0("fit_rq2_", x, "_partn_i"), readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq2_", x, "_partn_i.rds")))
    assign(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", x, "_si"), readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", x, "_si.rds")))
    assign(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", x, "_si_constr"), readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", x, "_si_constr.rds")))
    assign(paste0("lrt_rq2_mg_", x, "_si"), readRDS(paste0("models/lrt_rq2_mg_", x, "_si.rds")))
  }
}

### single-group lavaan models:
# custom function for parameter extraction
extract_lav_rq2_partn_i <- function(fit_obj) {
  name_obj <- as.character(substitute(fit_obj))
  name_outc <- name_obj %>% 
    str_remove("fit_rq2_") %>% 
    str_remove("_partn_i$")
  group_lab <- ifelse(str_detect(name_obj, "partn_i$"),
                      "Intermittently partnered",
                      "Consistently single")
  # use tidy() for extraction
  broom::tidy(fit_obj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("a0", "a1", "cis", "bi", "bs", "vi", "vs")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           group_fct = factor(group_lab, 
                            levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered"), 
                            labels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
    select(outc, group_fct, term = label, est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
           z_value = statistic, p_value = p.value, est_std = std.all)
}

# bind all model outputs together
rq2_summary_partn_i <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_avoi_rom_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_avoi_fri_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_avoi_mot_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_avoi_fat_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_anxi_glo_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_anxi_rom_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_anxi_fri_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_anxi_mot_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq2_partn_i(fit_rq2_anxi_fat_partn_i)
)

# Add labels
rq2_summary_partn_i <- rq2_summary_partn_i %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))#

### multi-group lavaan models
# custom function for parameter extraction 
extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i <- function(fit_obj, lrt_obj) {
  name_obj <- as.character(substitute(fit_obj))
  name_outc <- str_remove(name_obj, "fit_rq2_mg_") %>% 
    str_remove("_si")
  
  # extract LRT information
  lrt_tab <- as.data.frame(lrt_obj)
  lrt_chi <- lrt_tab$`Chisq diff`[2]
  lrt_df <- lrt_tab$`Df diff`[2]
  lrt_p <- lrt_tab$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
  
  # extract model parameters
  broom::tidy(fit_obj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("a0_s", "a0_p", "a1_s", "a1_p", "cis_s", "cis_p",
                        "bi_s", "bi_p", "bs_s", "bs_p", "vi_s", "vi_p", "vs_s", "vs_p")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           group_fct = case_when(str_detect(label, "_s$") ~ "Consistently single",
                                 str_detect(label, "_p$") ~ "Intermittently partnered", # p = means Intermittently here!
                                 TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      group_fct = factor(group_fct, levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered",
                                    "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE),
      lrt_chi = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_chi, NA),
      lrt_df = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_df, NA),
      lrt_p = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_p, NA)) %>% 
    select(outc, group_fct, term = label,
           est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
           z_value = statistic, p_value = p.value, est_std = std.all,
           lrt_chi, lrt_df, lrt_p)
}

# bind all model outputs together
rq2_summary_mg_partn_i <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_si, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_rom_si, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_rom_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fri_si, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_fri_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_mot_si, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_mot_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fat_si, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_fat_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_glo_si, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_glo_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_rom_si, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_rom_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fri_si, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_fri_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_mot_si, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_mot_si),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_partn_i(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fat_si, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_fat_si)
)

# Add labels
rq2_summary_mg_partn_i <- rq2_summary_mg_partn_i %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))
```

### Model fit

Fit statistics: single-group models  
-> These fit indices are very computationally expensive. I put them in a conditional chunk and load them as an RDS object in the next chunk.  

```{r calc-fit-rq2-partn-i}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_expensive) { # only run when we allow this in YAML heading

# model fit statistics: single-group models
rq2_fit_partn_i <- outcomes$short %>% 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(x) {
    bind_rows(
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq2_", x, "_partn_i"))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Intermittently partnered"))
  }) %>% 
  select(outc, group_fct, nobs, npar, AIC, BIC, cfi, rmsea, srmr) %>% 
  mutate(
    outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
    group_fct = factor(group_fct,
                       levels = c("Intermittently partnered"),
                       ordered = TRUE))

# save externally:
saveRDS(rq2_fit_partn_i, "model_fit/rq2_fit_partn_i.rds")
}
```

### Model diagnostics

- Did the model converge?  
- Did lavaan's internal check pass?  
- Are there inadmissible negative variances?  

#### Single-group models

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# diagnostics for the single-group RQ2 models (interm. partnered)
rq2_models_partn_i <- c("fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_i", "fit_rq2_avoi_rom_partn_i",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fri_partn_i", "fit_rq2_avoi_mot_partn_i",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fat_partn_i", "fit_rq2_anxi_glo_partn_i",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_rom_partn_i", "fit_rq2_anxi_fri_partn_i",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_mot_partn_i", "fit_rq2_anxi_fat_partn_i")

rq2_diagnostics_partn_i <- purrr::map_dfr(rq2_models_partn_i, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(parameterEstimates(fit)$op == "~~" &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$lhs == parameterEstimates(fit)$rhs &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$est < 0))
})

rq2_diagnostics_partn_i %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

#### Multi-group models

```{r}

rq2_mg_models_partn_i <- c("fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_si", "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_rom_si",

                   "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fat_si", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_glo_si",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_rom_si", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fri_si",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_mot_si", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fat_si")

rq2_mg_diagnostics_partn_i <- purrr::map_dfr(rq2_mg_models_partn_i, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(pe$op == "~~" &
                          pe$lhs == pe$rhs &
                          pe$est < 0))
})

rq2_mg_diagnostics_partn_i %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Compared to consistently single people, intermittently partnered people decreased to a greater extent in romantic attachment avoidance (while both starting in similar places). Both groups decreased significantly over time, but this decrease was more pronounced in the intermittently partnered people. This is similar to romantic attachment anxiety, where intermittently partnered people also decreased more, while starting at similar levels.    

It looks a bit different for mother-specific attachment avoidance: here, consistently single people decreased more over time than intermittently partnered people did. However, overall both groups are quite close to each other throughout (see confidence bands). This is also quite similar to our result comparing consistently single to consistently partnered people.     

No significant differences in slopes among the other domains. Level differences are quite pronounced for global avoidance (anxiety a bit less so) as well as friend-specific avoidance and anxiety.   
:::
