### Summary plot

Create plots for manuscript: start with extracting the parameters

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Custom function to extract model-implied trajectories from lavaan defined parameters
extract_rq2_plot_traject_partn_i <- function(fit, outcome_label) {
  parameterEstimates(fit, ci = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(op == ":=") %>%
    mutate(group = case_when(str_detect(lhs, "_s$") ~ "Consistently single",
                             str_detect(lhs, "_p$") ~ "Intermittently partnered"),
           month = as.numeric(str_extract(lhs, "(?<=t)\\d+")),
           time_years = month / 12,
           outcome = outcome_label) %>%
    select(outcome, group, month, time_years, estimate = est, ci_low = ci.lower, ci_high = ci.upper)
}

# Extract trajectories from all multi-group RQ2 models
plot_traject_list_rq2_partn_i <- list()
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
  fit <- readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_si.rds"))
  plot_traject_list_rq2_partn_i[[i]] <- extract_rq2_plot_traject_partn_i(fit, outcomes$maj[i])
}
plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i <- bind_rows(plot_traject_list_rq2_partn_i)

# Check extracted plotting dataframe
head(plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i)
table(plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i$outcome, plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i$group)

# create factor variables:
plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i <- plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i %>%
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes$maj, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
         group_fct = factor(group, levels = c("Consistently single", "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE))

# a bit tricky: handling variable y-axis ranges...
# Define common y-axis width across facets
y_range_rq2 <- 1.7
# Calculate facet-specific y-axis limits with equal zoom
plot_traject_limits_rq2_partn_i <- plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i %>%
  group_by(outc_fct) %>%
  summarise(y_mid = mean(range(c(ci_low, ci_high)))) %>%
  mutate(y_lower = y_mid - y_range_rq2 / 2,
         y_upper = y_mid + y_range_rq2 / 2)
# Create facet-specific y-axis scales with half-point breaks
y_scales_rq2_partn_i <- lapply(1:nrow(plot_traject_limits_rq2_partn_i), function(i) {
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(plot_traject_limits_rq2_partn_i$y_lower[i],
                                plot_traject_limits_rq2_partn_i$y_upper[i]),
                     breaks = seq(floor(plot_traject_limits_rq2_partn_i$y_lower[i] * 2) / 2,
                                  ceiling(plot_traject_limits_rq2_partn_i$y_upper[i] * 2) / 2,
                                  by = 0.5),
                     labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1))
})

# Create significance labels from LRT p-values
rq2_sig_labels_partn_i <- rq2_table_mg_partn_i_a %>%
  filter(term == "a1_s") %>%
  mutate(sig = case_when(lrt_p < .001 ~ "***",
                         lrt_p < .01 ~ "**",
                         lrt_p < .05 ~ "*",
                         TRUE ~ "")) %>%
  select(outc_fct, sig) %>% 
  mutate(outc_label = ifelse(sig == "", as.character(outc_fct), paste0(as.character(outc_fct), " (", sig, ")")))
# Add labelled outcome factor for plotting
plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i <- plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i %>%
  left_join(rq2_sig_labels_partn_i %>% select(outc_fct, outc_label), by = "outc_fct") %>%
  mutate(outc_fct_label = factor(outc_label, levels = unique(outc_label))) %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct_label = factor(outc_fct_label, levels = unique(outc_fct_label), ordered = TRUE))
```

Create and save plot: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Define custom group colours and linetypes
group_colors <- c("Consistently single" = "#008837", "Intermittently partnered" = "#6A3D9A")
group_linetypes <- c("Consistently single" = "solid", "Intermittently partnered" = "dotdash")

# Plot RQ2 model-implied trajectories with 95% confidence bands
plot_rq2_traject_partn_i <- ggplot(plot_traject_df_rq2_partn_i, aes(x = time_years, y = estimate, 
                                                     colour = group_fct, fill = group_fct,
                                                     linetype = group_fct)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), alpha = .20, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = group_linetypes) +
  facet_wrap(~outc_fct_label, ncol = 2, nrow = 5, scales = "free_y", dir = "v") +
  ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales(y = y_scales_rq2_partn_i) +
  labs(x = "Years since baseline", y = "Attachment domain (model-implied; 95% CI-band)", 
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         fill = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         linetype = guide_legend(title = "Group")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())

# save as pdf
pdf(width = 6.5, height = 7.5, "figures/rq2_traject_expl.pdf")
plot_rq2_traject_partn_i
dev.off()
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Main difference with the intermittently partnered group: Significant differences in romantic attachment, where intermittently partnered people start out more insecure (than the consistently partnered) but then become more secure, again, over time and to a greater extent that the consistently single people. This likely reflects the influence of forming new relationship(s).
:::

## RQ3: Co-Development of Attachment and Life Satisfaction (consistently & intermittently partnered)

From prereg: "In addition, for all attachment models, we will explore co-development between attachment and life satisfaction in (1) consistently partnered individuals and (2) intermittently partnered individuals."

We don't need to adjust the template. Same as above, we just use different groups.

### Template loop & extraction

Run loop over all 5 X 2 outcomes  

(Here, I suppress lavaan warnings in the html output, but they are very similar to the ones shown above for the example model. Below, I go into model diagnostics more systematically.)  

```{r rq3-loop-expl}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_models) { # we can toggle this on/off in the YAML heading
  
# loop across all attachment outcomes
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
  print(paste0("Running outcome: ", outcomes$maj[i]))

  # Fill bivariate LGCM template
  model_rq3 <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq3_template, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])

  # Outcome-specific missingness indicator -> added this mostly for parent-specific attachment
  missi_var <- paste0(outcomes$short[i], "_missi")
  
  # Fit model in consistently partnered people
  fit_rq3_partn_c <- lavaan::growth(model_rq3,
                                    data = df_atta_wide_partn_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                                    missing = "fiml",
                                    verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_c")), fit_rq3_partn_c))
  saveRDS(fit_rq3_partn_c, file = paste0("models/fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_c.rds"))

  # Fit model in intermittently partnered people
  fit_rq3_partn_i <- lavaan::growth(model_rq3,
                                    data = df_atta_wide_partn_i %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                                    missing = "fiml",
                                    verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_i")), fit_rq3_partn_i))
  saveRDS(fit_rq3_partn_i, file = paste0("models/fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_i.rds"))
}
}
```

Create summary table of all effects of interest: parameter extraction  
... this is based on the broom::tidy() method with unstandardized parameters  

```{r rq3-load-extract-expl}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Load saved models when run_models = FALSE
if (!params$run_models) {
  for (x in outcomes$short) {
    assign(paste0("fit_rq3_", x, "_partn_c"), readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq3_", x, "_partn_c.rds")))
    assign(paste0("fit_rq3_", x, "_partn_i"), readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq3_", x, "_partn_i.rds")))
  }
}

# custom function for parameter extraction from bivariate LGCMs
# same as above

# bind all model outputs together -> Consistently partnered
rq3_summary_partn_c <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_glo_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_rom_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fri_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_mot_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fat_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_glo_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_rom_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fri_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_mot_partn_c),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fat_partn_c)
)
# Add labels
rq3_summary_partn_c <- rq3_summary_partn_c %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short,
                           labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))

# bind all model outputs together -> Intermittently partnered
rq3_summary_partn_i <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_glo_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_rom_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fri_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_mot_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fat_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_glo_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_rom_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fri_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_mot_partn_i),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fat_partn_i)
)
# Add labels
rq3_summary_partn_i <- rq3_summary_partn_i %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short,
                           labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))
```

For the preregistered effects of interest, I use lavaan::standardizedSolution(). For the cross-construct latent growth-factor covariances, standardization yields correlations rather than covariances. The standardized estimates have their own SEs, CIs, and p-values, which can differ slightly from those of the corresponding unstandardized covariances. This matches the preregistration: “The main effects of interest are the cross-construct intercept-slope correlations and slope-slope correlations.”  

The standardized effect size is always the same as the est_std / std.all one from broom::tidy(), though.  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Extract standardized slope-slope correlation and CI
# same function as above

# Extract all RQ3 slope-slope correlations -> Consistently partnered
rq3_models_partn_c <- c("fit_rq3_avoi_glo_partn_c", "fit_rq3_avoi_rom_partn_c",
                "fit_rq3_avoi_fri_partn_c", "fit_rq3_avoi_mot_partn_c",
                "fit_rq3_avoi_fat_partn_c", "fit_rq3_anxi_glo_partn_c",
                "fit_rq3_anxi_rom_partn_c", "fit_rq3_anxi_fri_partn_c",
                "fit_rq3_anxi_mot_partn_c", "fit_rq3_anxi_fat_partn_c")

rq3_extracted_cross_partn_c <- bind_rows(lapply(rq3_models_partn_c, function(x) {
  extract_rq3_cross_std(get(x), x)
})) %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(domain_fct = factor(str_remove(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety): "), 
                             levels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father"),
                             ordered = TRUE),
         pred_fct = factor(str_extract(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety)"), 
                           levels = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety"),
                           ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, term) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, domain_fct, pred_fct)

# Extract all RQ3 slope-slope correlations -> Intermittently partnered
rq3_models_partn_i <- c("fit_rq3_avoi_glo_partn_i", "fit_rq3_avoi_rom_partn_i",
                        "fit_rq3_avoi_fri_partn_i", "fit_rq3_avoi_mot_partn_i",
                        "fit_rq3_avoi_fat_partn_i", "fit_rq3_anxi_glo_partn_i",
                        "fit_rq3_anxi_rom_partn_i", "fit_rq3_anxi_fri_partn_i",
                        "fit_rq3_anxi_mot_partn_i", "fit_rq3_anxi_fat_partn_i")

rq3_extracted_cross_partn_i <- bind_rows(lapply(rq3_models_partn_i, function(x) {
  extract_rq3_cross_std(get(x), x)
})) %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(domain_fct = factor(str_remove(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety): "), 
                             levels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father"),
                             ordered = TRUE),
         pred_fct = factor(str_extract(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety)"), 
                           levels = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety"),
                           ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, term) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, domain_fct, pred_fct)
```

### Model fit

Fit statistics: consistently partnered  
-> These fit indices are very computationally expensive. I put them in a conditional chunk and load them as an RDS object in the next chunk.  

```{r calc-fit-rq3-partn-c}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_expensive) { # only run when we allow this in YAML heading
  
# model fit statistics: single-group models -> consistently partnered
rq3_fit_partn_c <- outcomes$short %>% 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(x) {
    bind_rows(
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq3_", x, "_partn_c"))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Consistently partnered"))
  }) %>% 
  select(outc, group_fct, nobs, npar, AIC, BIC, cfi, rmsea, srmr) %>% 
  mutate(
    outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
    group_fct = factor(group_fct,
                       levels = c("Consistently single",
                                  "Consistently partnered",
                                  "Intermittently partnered"),
                       ordered = TRUE))

# save externally:
saveRDS(rq3_fit_partn_c, "model_fit/rq3_fit_partn_c.rds")
}
```

Show fit indices table: 
```{r show-fit-rq3-partn-c}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false

rq3_fit_partn_c <- readRDS("model_fit/rq3_fit_partn_c.rds")

rq3_fit_partn_c %>% select(-outc) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, everything()) %>% 
  kable(digits = 3)
```

Fit statistics: intermittently partnered

```{r calc-fit-rq3-partn-i}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_expensive) { # only run when we allow this in YAML heading
  
# model fit statistics: single-group models
rq3_fit_partn_i <- outcomes$short %>% 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(x) {
    bind_rows(
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq3_", x, "_partn_i"))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Intermittently partnered"))
  }) %>% 
  select(outc, group_fct, nobs, npar, AIC, BIC, cfi, rmsea, srmr) %>% 
  mutate(
    outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
    group_fct = factor(group_fct,
                       levels = c("Consistently single",
                                  "Consistently partnered",
                                  "Intermittently partnered"),
                       ordered = TRUE))

# save externally:
saveRDS(rq3_fit_partn_i, "model_fit/rq3_fit_partn_i.rds")
}
```

Show fit indices table: 

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Somewhat better fit here in both groups than in the confirmatory models with the single people. Sample size is more than double here, though. That may play a role.

### Model diagnostics

- Did the model converge?  
- Did lavaan's internal check pass?  
- Are there inadmissible negative variances?  

Diagnostics: consistently partnered  
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# diagnostics for all single-group RQ3 models
rq3_diagnostics_partn_c <- purrr::map_dfr(rq3_models_partn_c, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(parameterEstimates(fit)$op == "~~" &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$lhs == parameterEstimates(fit)$rhs &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$est < 0))
})

rq3_diagnostics_partn_c %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

Diagnostics: intermittently partnered
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# diagnostics for all single-group RQ3 models
rq3_diagnostics_partn_i <- purrr::map_dfr(rq3_models_partn_i, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(parameterEstimates(fit)$op == "~~" &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$lhs == parameterEstimates(fit)$rhs &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$est < 0))
})

rq3_diagnostics_partn_i %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
All looking good!     
:::

### Summary tables

#### Consistently partnered 

Latent intercept and slope factors: "alpha0" (a0 = attach, w0 = life sat) & "alpha1" (a1 = attach, w1 = life sat): 

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_partn_c_a <- rq3_summary_partn_c %>% 
  filter(term=="a0" | term=="a1" | term=="w0" | term=="w1") %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, group_fct, term) %>% 
  mutate(sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, sig, est_std)

rq3_table_partn_c_a %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 4, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_partn_c_a))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Compared to the consistently single people, the consistently partnered people have higher life satisfaction (intercept) and also increase more in life satisfaction (slope).  

In most attachment domains (esp. global & romantic), consistently partnered people are more securely attached (lower avoidance and anxiety). Descriptively, consistently single people also become more securely attached at higher rates than partnered people in most domains, but as we saw above, these differences are only seldomly significant. 
:::

Latent intercept / slope variances & covariance - general terminology:  
- (a) = attachment  
- (w) = well-being (life satisf.)  
- (c) = covariance (or: correlation in the standardized solution)    
- (v) = variance  
- (i) = latent intercept  
- (s) = latent slope   

Cross-construct correlations (which are most relevant for the hypotheses):  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_partn_c_cross <- rq3_extracted_cross_partn_c %>% 
  filter(term %in% c("cii", "cis_aw", "cis_wa", "css")) %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, term) %>% 
  mutate(group = "Consistently partnered", 
         sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, sig)

rq3_table_partn_c_cross %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 4, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_partn_c_cross))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Pretty similar to the singles we examined above. The intercept-intercept correlations are all negative and significant (*p* < .001): With higher attachment insecurity (both avoidance and anxiety), people have lower life satisfaction.  

The intercept-slope correlations are, again, a bit more varied but mostly not significant. However, here in the consistently partnered people a few more of the correlations between intercept (attachment) and slope (life sat) are significant and positive: with more insecure attachment (esp. anxiety), people increased more in life satisfaction.  

For slope-slope correlations, see below!  
:::

Focus on parameter that is relevant to hypothesis: slope-slope correlation (standardized solution)


::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}

### Summary plot

We're plotting the standardized effects (i.e., slope-slope correlations).  

#### Consistently partnered

Create and save plot: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Plot standardized slope-slope correlations -> Consistently partnered
plot_rq3_css_partn_c <- ggplot(rq3_extracted_cross_partn_c %>% filter(term=="css"), 
                               aes(x = est, y = forcats::fct_rev(domain_fct),
                                   colour = forcats::fct_rev(pred_fct), 
                                   shape = forcats::fct_rev(pred_fct))) +
  geom_rect(data = bg_df_rq3,
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = NULL),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = bg_df_rq3$fill,
            alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi), 
                 height = 0.3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6),
                 linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Avoidance" = "#D55E00", "Anxiety" = "#0072B2"),
                      breaks = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Avoidance" = 17, "Anxiety" = 16),
                     breaks = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.60, 0.20), 
                     breaks = seq(-0.60, 0.20, by = 0.20),
                     labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
                     oob = scales::oob_keep) +
  labs(x = "Slope-slope correlation (95% CI)", 
       y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3), panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Attachment variable"),
         shape = guide_legend(title = "Attachment variable"))

# save as pdf
pdf(width = 6, height = 4.5, "figures/rq3_plot_css_partn_c.pdf")
plot_rq3_css_partn_c
dev.off()
```

```{r rq3-summary-plot-partn-c-show}
#| fig-height: 4.5
```

```{r}
  rq3_extracted_cross %>% mutate(group = "Consistently single"),

  rq3_extracted_cross_partn_i %>% mutate(group = "Intermittently partnered")
) %>%

# Define custom group colours
group_colors <- c("Consistently single" = "#008837", "Consistently partnered" = "#A23E48", 
                  "Intermittently partnered" = "#6A3D9A")

# Plot standardized slope-slope correlations across groups
plot_rq3_css_all <- ggplot(rq3_extracted_cross_all %>% filter(term=="css"), 
                           aes(x = est, y = forcats::fct_rev(group_fct), 
                               colour = forcats::fct_rev(group_fct), 
                               shape = forcats::fct_rev(group_fct))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi), height = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors, breaks = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", "Intermittently partnered")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Consistently single" = 16, "Consistently partnered" = 17, "Intermittently partnered" = 15), breaks = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", "Intermittently partnered")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.60, 0.20), breaks = seq(-0.60, 0.20, by = 0.20), labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1), oob = scales::oob_keep) +
  facet_wrap(~ outc_fct, ncol = 2, nrow = 5, dir = "v") +
  labs(x = "Slope-slope correlation (95% CI)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Group", override.aes = list(shape = c(16, 17, 15))), shape = "none") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10), strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3), panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

# save as pdf
pdf(width = 6, height = 7, "figures/rq3_plot_css_all.pdf")
plot_rq3_css_all
dev.off()
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Global attachment has relatively similar co-development across groups. However, in the specific domains some important differences emerge: romantic avoidance is much more relevant for the partnered groups than the singles. Also, some more subtle differences for best-friend attachment and mother/father. 
:::

# Robustness checks

## LGCM re-run as multilevel models

Comparing change in consistently single people vs. consistently partnered people  

A few changes to long df: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false

df_atta_mlm <- df_atta %>% 
  filter(group_fct!="Intermittently partnered people") %>% 
  filter(time_month_rd %in% c(0:29)) %>% # same restriction as in the SEM -> too much attrition in later waves
  mutate(single = ifelse(group_fct=="Consistently partnered people", 0, 1))
# this dummy now contrasts consistently partnered people (= reference group) with consistently single people
```

### Example model 

Example model first:  
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

fit_rq2_lmer_avoi_glo <- lmerTest::lmer(
  avoi_glo ~ time_month_rd * single + age_base_z * single + (1 + time_month_rd | pid),
  data = df_atta_mlm, REML = FALSE)

summary(fit_rq2_lmer_avoi_glo)
```

### Run loop

Run all outcomes in a loop:
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq2_lmer_models <- list()

for (i in seq_along(outcomes$short)) {
  out <- outcomes$short[i]
  message("Running outcome: ", out)
  
  model <- lmerTest::lmer(
    as.formula(paste0(out, " ~ time_month_rd * single + age_base_z * single + (1 + time_month_rd | pid)")),
    data = df_atta_mlm,
    REML = FALSE
  )
  
  rq2_lmer_models[[out]] <- model
  assign(paste0("fit_rq2_lmer_", out), model)
  saveRDS(model, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_lmer_", out, ".rds"))
}
```

Extract and combine the parameters of interest
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Satterthwaite-based df and p.value
rq2_lmer_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(rq2_lmer_models, ~broom.mixed::tidy(.x, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term %in% c("time_month_rd", "single", "time_month_rd:single", "age_base_z", "age_base_z:single")) %>%
  mutate(outc = .y,
    n_persons = dplyr::n_distinct(model.frame(.x)$pid),
    n_obs = nrow(model.frame(.x)))) %>% 
  rename(est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high, p_value = p.value) %>%
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))

# group differences in slopes
rq2_lmer_slope_diff <- rq2_lmer_summary %>% 
  filter(term == "time_month_rd:single") %>% 
  select(outc, outc_fct, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, n_persons, n_obs) 
```

### Results table

Focusing on the effect of interest: cross-level interaction of time (in months) and group (partnered vs. single)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq2_lmer_slope_diff %>% select(-1) %>% 
  mutate(sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  relocate(sig, .after = p_value) %>% 
  kable(digits = 3)
```

To compare effect sizes with lavaan models: both now use 30 months of data
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq2_lmer_slopes <- purrr::imap_dfr(rq2_lmer_models, function(model, model_name) {
  b <- lme4::fixef(model)
  V <- as.matrix(vcov(model))
  
  slope_p <- b["time_month_rd"]
  se_p <- sqrt(V["time_month_rd", "time_month_rd"])
  
  slope_s <- b["time_month_rd"] + b["time_month_rd:single"]
  se_s <- sqrt(V["time_month_rd", "time_month_rd"] +
               V["time_month_rd:single", "time_month_rd:single"] +
               2 * V["time_month_rd", "time_month_rd:single"])
  
  tibble::tibble(
    outc = gsub("^fit_rq2_lmer_", "", model_name),
    group = c("Consistently partnered", "Consistently single"),
    change_30m = c(slope_p, slope_s) * 30,
    ci_lo = c(slope_p - 1.96 * se_p, slope_s - 1.96 * se_s) * 30,
    ci_hi = c(slope_p + 1.96 * se_p, slope_s + 1.96 * se_s) * 30
  )
})

rq2_lmer_slopes %>% 
  mutate(change_30m = sprintf("%.2f", change_30m),
         ci_95 = paste0("[", sprintf("%.2f", ci_lo), ", ", sprintf("%.2f", ci_hi), "]")) %>% 
  left_join(rq2_lmer_summary %>% distinct(outc, outc_fct), by = "outc") %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, factor(group, levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered"),
                           labels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered"))) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group, change_30m, ci_95) %>% 
  kable(col.names = c("Outcome", "Group", "30-month change", "95% CI"))
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Quite similar to the lavaan() LGCM! The significance testing is bit more liberal here compared to the LRT method (matching *p* < .10 in the LRTs...). Effect sizes are also quite similar. Main difference probably lies in the FIML method for dealing with missingness which is not applied here in the MLM.
:::

### Summary plot

Construct df for plot: 

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# predict at every month and separately for the two groups
plot_traject_df_rq2_lmer <- 
  purrr::imap_dfr(rq2_lmer_models, 
                  ~ggeffects::ggpredict(.x, terms = c("time_month_rd [0:29]", "single [0,1]")) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(outc = .y))

plot_traject_df_rq2_lmer <- plot_traject_df_rq2_lmer %>%
  mutate(group_fct = factor(group, levels = c(0, 1),
                            labels = c("Consistently partnered", "Consistently single"),
                            ordered = TRUE),
         outc_fct_label = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short,
                                 labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
         time_years = x / 12)

# significance stars in labels
rq2_lmer_stars <- rq2_lmer_summary %>% 
  filter(term == "time_month_rd:single") %>% 
  mutate(stars = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ ""),
         stars = ifelse(stars == "", "", paste0(" (", stars, ")"))) %>% 
  select(outc, stars)
# Add labelled outcome factor for plotting
plot_traject_df_rq2_lmer <- plot_traject_df_rq2_lmer %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  left_join(rq2_lmer_stars, by = "outc") %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct_label = ifelse(stars == "", as.character(outc_fct), paste0(as.character(outc_fct), stars)),
         outc_fct_label = factor(outc_fct_label, levels = unique(outc_fct_label), ordered = TRUE))

# Define common y-axis width across facets
y_range_rq2_lmer <- 1.7
plot_traject_limits_rq2_lmer <- plot_traject_df_rq2_lmer %>%
  group_by(outc_fct_label) %>%
  summarise(y_mid = mean(range(c(conf.low, conf.high))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(y_lower = y_mid - y_range_rq2_lmer / 2,
         y_upper = y_mid + y_range_rq2_lmer / 2)

y_scales_rq2_lmer <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(plot_traject_limits_rq2_lmer)), function(i) {
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(plot_traject_limits_rq2_lmer$y_lower[i],
               plot_traject_limits_rq2_lmer$y_upper[i]),
    breaks = seq(floor(plot_traject_limits_rq2_lmer$y_lower[i] * 2) / 2,
                 ceiling(plot_traject_limits_rq2_lmer$y_upper[i] * 2) / 2,
                 by = 0.5),
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)
  )
})
```

Create and save plot: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

group_colors <- c("Consistently single" = "#008837", "Consistently partnered" = "#A23E48")
group_linetypes <- c("Consistently single" = "solid", "Consistently partnered" = "longdash")

# Plot RQ2 MLM model-implied trajectories with 95% confidence bands
plot_rq2_traject_lmer <- ggplot(plot_traject_df_rq2_lmer, aes(x = time_years, y = predicted,
                                                               colour = group_fct, fill = group_fct,
                                                               linetype = group_fct)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = .20, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors, breaks = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors, breaks = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = group_linetypes, breaks = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered")) +
  facet_wrap(~outc_fct_label, ncol = 2, nrow = 5, scales = "free_y", dir = "v") +
  ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales(y = y_scales_rq2_lmer) +
  labs(x = "Years since baseline", y = "Attachment domain (model-implied; 95% CI-band)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         fill = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         linetype = guide_legend(title = "Group")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())

pdf(width = 6.5, height = 7.5, "figures/rq2_traject_lmer.pdf")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
These trajectories look remarkably similar to the SEM/lavaan ones. At first glance, the biggest difference is maybe the tiny difference in the singles' slope for father-specific anxiety.   

The significance evaluation is slightly different here and a bit more liberal (this is typical, in my experience). Therefore, we also get significant slope differences (i.e., cross-level interactions) for global anxiety and romantic avoidance.  
:::

## LGCM but only up to 24 months 

For this check, the idea is that the later months of data are relatively sparse and that most participants finished the study within 24 months. Our confirmatory models above (using 30 out of potentially 41 available months) aimed to strike a compromise and use rather more of these later months. Now we aim to be a bit more conservative and try to model the period where we definitely have sufficient observations.  


### RQ2 models

#### Adjust templates

```{r rq2-loop-templ-24}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Define 24-month assessment window
n_waves <- 24
times <- sprintf("%02d", 0:(n_waves - 1))
outcome_vars <- paste0("outcome_t", times)

# Intercept loadings
i_loadings <- paste0("1*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Slope loadings (scaled 0 to 1 across 24 months)
s_values <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_waves)
s_loadings <- paste0(round(s_values, 5), "*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Residual variance labels
residuals <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ res_", times, "*", outcome_vars, collapse = "\n")

# Model-implied trajectory parameters
trajectory_estimates <- paste0("pred_t", times, " := a0 + a1*", round(s_values, 5), collapse = "\n")

# Single-group LGCM template
rq2_template_24m <- paste0('
# Define intercept and slope factors
i =~ ', i_loadings, '

s =~ ', s_loadings, '

# Regress latent growth factors on baseline age
i ~ bi*age_base_z
s ~ bs*age_base_z

# Mean structure
i ~ a0*1
s ~ a1*1

# Variance structure
i ~~ vi*i
s ~~ vs*s
i ~~ cis*s

# Model-implied trajectories (assuming age_base_z = 0, i.e., sample-average baseline age)
', trajectory_estimates, '

# Residual variances
', residuals, '
')

# Residual variance labels (group-specific)
residuals_multi <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ c(\"r", times, "_s\", \"r", times, "_p\")*", outcome_vars, collapse = "\n")

# Model-implied trajectory parameters
trajectory_estimates_multi <- paste0("pred_t", times, "_s := a0_s + a1_s*", round(s_values, 5),
                                     "\n",
                                     "pred_t", times, "_p := a0_p + a1_p*", round(s_values, 5), collapse = "\n")

# Multi-group LGCM template
rq2_template_multi_24m <- paste0('
# Define intercept and slope factors
i =~ ', i_loadings, '

s =~ ', s_loadings, '

# Regress latent growth factors on baseline age
i ~ c("bi_s", "bi_p")*age_base_z
s ~ c("bs_s", "bs_p")*age_base_z

# Mean structure
i ~ c("a0_s", "a0_p")*1
s ~ c("a1_s", "a1_p")*1

# Variance structure
i ~~ c("vi_s", "vi_p")*i
s ~~ c("vs_s", "vs_p")*s
i ~~ c("cis_s", "cis_p")*s

# Model-implied trajectories (assuming age_base_z = 0, i.e., sample-average baseline age)
', trajectory_estimates_multi, '

# Residual variances
', residuals_multi, '

')

# Constrained multi-group template
rq2_template_multi_constr_24m <- stringr::str_replace(rq2_template_multi_24m, 
                                                       's ~ c\\("a1_s", "a1_p"\\)\\*1', 's ~ a1*1')
rq2_template_multi_constr_24m <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr_24m, 'a1_s', 'a1')
rq2_template_multi_constr_24m <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr_24m, 'a1_p', 'a1')
```

#### Template loop & extraction

Run loop over all 5 X 2 outcomes  

(Here, I suppress lavaan warnings in the html output, but they are very similar to the ones shown above for the example model. Below, I go into model diagnostics more systematically.)  

```{r rq2-loop-24}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_models) { # we can toggle this on/off in the YAML heading
  
# Loop across all attachment outcomes
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
  print(paste0("Running outcome: ", outcomes$maj[i]))
  
  # Outcome-specific missingness indicator -> added this mostly for parent-specific attachment
  missi_var <- paste0(outcomes$short[i], "_missi")
  
  # Step 1: fill single-group model template (2x, 1 for single, 1 for partnered)
  print("-> Step 1")
  model_rq2_24m <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_24m, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_24m <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_24m,
                                data = df_atta_wide_single_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                                missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m")), fit_rq2_24m))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_24m, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m.rds"))
  
  fit_rq2_partn_c_24m <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_24m,
                                        data = df_atta_wide_partn_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                                        missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_c_24m")), fit_rq2_partn_c_24m))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_partn_c_24m, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_", outcomes$short[i], "_partn_c_24m.rds"))

  # Step 2: fill free multigroup model template
  print("-> Step 2")
  model_rq2_multi_24m <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_24m, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_multi_24m <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_multi_24m,
                                      data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0) %>% 
                                        arrange(group_fct),
                                      group = "group_fct",
                                      missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m")), fit_rq2_multi_24m))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_multi_24m, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m.rds"))

  # Step 3: fill constrained multigroup model template
  print("-> Step 3")
  model_rq2_multi_constr_24m <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq2_template_multi_constr_24m, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  fit_rq2_multi_constr_24m <- lavaan::growth(model_rq2_multi_constr_24m,
                                             data = df_atta_wide_single_partn_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0) %>% 
                                               arrange(group_fct),
                                             group = "group_fct",
                                             missing = "fiml", verbose = FALSE)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_constr_24m")),
            fit_rq2_multi_constr_24m))
  saveRDS(fit_rq2_multi_constr_24m, file = paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", 
                                                  outcomes$short[i], "_constr_24m.rds"))

  # Step 4: likelihood ratio test: free vs constrained slopes
  print("-> Step 4")
  lrt_24m <- anova(fit_rq2_multi_24m, fit_rq2_multi_constr_24m)
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("lrt_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m")), lrt_24m))
  saveRDS(lrt_24m, file = paste0("models/lrt_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m.rds"))
}
}
```

First, parameter extraction

```{r rq2-load-extract-24}
    assign(paste0("lrt_rq2_mg_", x, "_24m"), readRDS(paste0("models/lrt_rq2_mg_", x, "_24m.rds")))
  }
}

### single-group lavaan models:
# custom function for parameter extraction
extract_lav_rq2_24m <- function(fit_obj) {
  name_obj <- as.character(substitute(fit_obj))
  name_outc <- name_obj %>% 
    str_remove("fit_rq2_") %>% 
    str_remove("_partn_c") %>% 
    str_remove("_24m")
  group_lab <- ifelse(str_detect(name_obj, "partn_c"),
                      "Consistently partnered",
                      "Consistently single")
  # use tidy() for extraction
  broom::tidy(fit_obj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("a0", "a1", "cis", "bi", "bs", "vi", "vs")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           group_fct = factor(group_lab, 
                            levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered"), 
                            labels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered", 
                                       "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
    select(outc, group_fct, term = label, est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
           z_value = statistic, p_value = p.value, est_std = std.all)
}

# bind all model outputs together
rq2_summary_single_24m <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_glo_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_rom_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_fri_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_mot_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_fat_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_anxi_glo_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_anxi_rom_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_anxi_fri_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_anxi_mot_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_anxi_fat_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_c_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_rom_partn_c_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_fri_partn_c_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_mot_partn_c_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_24m(fit_rq2_avoi_fat_partn_c_24m),

# Add labels

### multi-group lavaan models
# custom function for parameter extraction 
extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m <- function(fit_obj, lrt_obj) {
  name_obj <- as.character(substitute(fit_obj))
  name_outc <- str_remove(name_obj, "fit_rq2_mg_") %>% str_remove("_24m")
  
  # extract LRT information
  lrt_tab <- as.data.frame(lrt_obj)
  lrt_chi <- lrt_tab$`Chisq diff`[2]
  lrt_df <- lrt_tab$`Df diff`[2]
  lrt_p <- lrt_tab$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
  
  # extract model parameters
  broom::tidy(fit_obj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
    filter(label %in% c("a0_s", "a0_p", "a1_s", "a1_p", "cis_s", "cis_p",
                        "bi_s", "bi_p", "bs_s", "bs_p", "vi_s", "vi_p", "vs_s", "vs_p")) %>% 
    mutate(outc = name_outc,
           group_fct = case_when(str_detect(label, "_s$") ~ "Consistently single",
                                 str_detect(label, "_p$") ~ "Consistently partnered",
                                 TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      group_fct = factor(group_fct, levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered",
                                    "Intermittently partnered"), ordered = TRUE),
      lrt_chi = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_chi, NA),
      lrt_df = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_df, NA),
      lrt_p = ifelse(str_detect(label, "^a1_"), lrt_p, NA)) %>% 
    select(outc, group_fct, term = label,
           est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
           z_value = statistic, p_value = p.value, est_std = std.all,
           lrt_chi, lrt_df, lrt_p)
}

# bind all model outputs together
rq2_summary_mg_24m <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_rom_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_rom_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fri_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_fri_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_mot_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_mot_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fat_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_avoi_fat_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_glo_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_glo_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_rom_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_rom_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fri_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_fri_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_mot_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_mot_24m),
  extract_lav_rq2_mg_24m(fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fat_24m, lrt_rq2_mg_anxi_fat_24m)
)

# Add labels
rq2_summary_mg_24m <- rq2_summary_mg_24m %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))
```

#### Model fit

Fit statistics: single-group models  
-> These fit indices are very computationally expensive. I put them in a conditional chunk and load them as an RDS object in the next chunk.  

```{r calc-fit-rq2-24m}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_expensive) { # only run when we allow this in YAML heading

# model fit statistics: single-group models
rq2_fit_single_24m <- outcomes$short %>% 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(x) {
    bind_rows(
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq2_", x, "_24m"))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Consistently single"),
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq2_", x, "_partn_c_24m"))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Consistently partnered"))
  }) %>% 
  select(outc, group_fct, nobs, npar, AIC, BIC, cfi, rmsea, srmr) %>% 
  mutate(
    outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
    group_fct = factor(group_fct,
                       levels = c("Consistently single",
                                  "Consistently partnered",
                                  "Intermittently partnered"),
                       ordered = TRUE))

# save externally:
saveRDS(rq2_fit_single_24m, "model_fit/rq2_fit_single_24m.rds")
}
```

#### Model diagnostics

- Did the model converge?  
- Did lavaan's internal check pass?  
- Are there inadmissible negative variances?  

##### Single-group models

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# diagnostics for all single-group and partnered RQ2 models
rq2_models_24m <- c("fit_rq2_avoi_glo_24m", "fit_rq2_avoi_rom_24m",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fri_24m", "fit_rq2_avoi_mot_24m",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fat_24m", "fit_rq2_anxi_glo_24m",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_rom_24m", "fit_rq2_anxi_fri_24m",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_mot_24m", "fit_rq2_anxi_fat_24m",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_glo_partn_c_24m", "fit_rq2_avoi_rom_partn_c_24m",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fri_partn_c_24m", "fit_rq2_avoi_mot_partn_c_24m",
                "fit_rq2_avoi_fat_partn_c_24m", "fit_rq2_anxi_glo_partn_c_24m",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_rom_partn_c_24m", "fit_rq2_anxi_fri_partn_c_24m",
                "fit_rq2_anxi_mot_partn_c_24m", "fit_rq2_anxi_fat_partn_c_24m")

rq2_diagnostics_24m <- purrr::map_dfr(rq2_models_24m, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(parameterEstimates(fit)$op == "~~" &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$lhs == parameterEstimates(fit)$rhs &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$est < 0))
})

rq2_diagnostics_24m %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

##### Multi-group models

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq2_mg_models_24m <- c("fit_rq2_mg_avoi_glo_24m", "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_rom_24m",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fri_24m", "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_mot_24m",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_avoi_fat_24m", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_glo_24m",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_rom_24m", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fri_24m",
                   "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_mot_24m", "fit_rq2_mg_anxi_fat_24m")

rq2_mg_diagnostics_24m <- purrr::map_dfr(rq2_mg_models_24m, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(pe$op == "~~" &
                          pe$lhs == pe$rhs &
                          pe$est < 0))
})

rq2_mg_diagnostics_24m %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
All good here.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Quite similar estimates, overall! The main difference for significance testing is that we also find significant slope differences in global anxiety here (at *p* < .05; this was *p* = .071 in the 30-month model). Partnered people decrease more in global anxiety than singles.  

Otherwise, pretty similar. The 30-m. model tends to estimate somewhat larger attachment changes than the 24-m. model.  
:::

#### Summary plot

Create plots for manuscript: start with extracting the parameters

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Custom function to extract model-implied trajectories from lavaan defined parameters
# same function as above

# Extract trajectories from all multi-group RQ2 models
plot_traject_list_rq2_24m <- list()
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
  fit <- readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq2_mg_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m.rds"))
  plot_traject_list_rq2_24m[[i]] <- extract_rq2_plot_traject(fit, outcomes$maj[i])
}
plot_traject_df_rq2_24m <- bind_rows(plot_traject_list_rq2_24m)

# Check extracted plotting dataframe
head(plot_traject_df_rq2_24m)
table(plot_traject_df_rq2_24m$outcome, plot_traject_df_rq2_24m$group, useNA = "always")

# create factor variables:
plot_traject_df_rq2_24m <- plot_traject_df_rq2_24m %>%
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes$maj, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
         group_fct = factor(group, levels = c("Consistently single", "Consistently partnered"), ordered = TRUE))

# a bit tricky: handling variable y-axis ranges...
# Define common y-axis width across facets
y_range_rq2 <- 1.7
# Calculate facet-specific y-axis limits with equal zoom
plot_traject_limits_rq2_24m <- plot_traject_df_rq2_24m %>%
  group_by(outc_fct) %>%
  summarise(y_mid = mean(range(c(ci_low, ci_high)))) %>%
  mutate(y_lower = y_mid - y_range_rq2 / 2,
         y_upper = y_mid + y_range_rq2 / 2)
# Create facet-specific y-axis scales with half-point breaks
y_scales_rq2_24m <- lapply(1:nrow(plot_traject_limits_rq2_24m), function(i) {
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(plot_traject_limits_rq2_24m$y_lower[i],
                                plot_traject_limits_rq2_24m$y_upper[i]),
                     breaks = seq(floor(plot_traject_limits_rq2_24m$y_lower[i] * 2) / 2,
                                  ceiling(plot_traject_limits_rq2_24m$y_upper[i] * 2) / 2,
                                  by = 0.5),
                     labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1))
})

# Create significance labels from LRT p-values
rq2_sig_labels_24m <- rq2_table_mg_24m_a %>%
  filter(term == "a1_s") %>%
  mutate(sig = case_when(lrt_p < .001 ~ "***",
                         lrt_p < .01 ~ "**",
                         lrt_p < .05 ~ "*",
                         TRUE ~ "")) %>%
  select(outc_fct, sig) %>% 
  mutate(outc_label = ifelse(sig == "", as.character(outc_fct), paste0(as.character(outc_fct), " (", sig, ")")))
# Add labelled outcome factor for plotting
plot_traject_df_rq2_24m <- plot_traject_df_rq2_24m %>%
  left_join(rq2_sig_labels_24m %>% select(outc_fct, outc_label), by = "outc_fct") %>%
  mutate(outc_fct_label = factor(outc_label, levels = unique(outc_label))) %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct_label = factor(outc_fct_label, levels = unique(outc_fct_label), ordered = TRUE))
```

Create and save plot: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

group_colors <- c("Consistently single" = "#008837", "Consistently partnered" = "#A23E48")
group_linetypes <- c("Consistently single" = "solid", "Consistently partnered" = "longdash")

# Plot RQ2 model-implied trajectories with 95% confidence bands
plot_rq2_traject_24m <- ggplot(plot_traject_df_rq2_24m, aes(x = time_years, y = estimate, 
                                                     colour = group_fct, fill = group_fct,
                                                     linetype = group_fct)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), alpha = .20, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = group_linetypes) +
  facet_wrap(~outc_fct_label, ncol = 2, nrow = 5, scales = "free_y", dir = "v") +
  ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales(y = y_scales_rq2_24m) +
  labs(x = "Years since baseline", y = "Attachment domain (model-implied; 95% CI-band)", 
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         fill = guide_legend(title = "Group"),
         linetype = guide_legend(title = "Group")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())

# save as pdf
pdf(width = 6.5, height = 7.5, "figures/rq2_traject_24m.pdf")
plot_rq2_traject_24m
dev.off()
```

Show plot: 
```{r rq2-summary-plot-24m-show}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| cache: false

plot_rq2_traject_24m
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
The trajectories look remarkably similar to the 30-month version across all domains! The main analytic difference concerns the significant evaluation for global anxiety. However, the trajectories themselves are still very similar (for the matching time period of the first 24 months, I mean).
:::

### RQ3 models

#### Adjust templates

```{r rq3-loop-templ-24}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Define number of assessment waves
n_waves <- 24  # t00 to t23

# Create variable names
times <- sprintf("%02d", 0:(n_waves - 1))
outcome_vars <- paste0("outcome_t", times)
swb_vars <- paste0("swb_t", times)

# Intercept loadings
i_loadings_out <- paste0("1*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")
i_loadings_swb <- paste0("1*", swb_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Slope loadings (scaled 0 to 1)
s_values <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_waves)
s_loadings_out <- paste0(round(s_values, 5), "*", outcome_vars, collapse = " + ")
s_loadings_swb <- paste0(round(s_values, 5), "*", swb_vars, collapse = " + ")

# Residual variance labels
res_out <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ ra", times, "*", outcome_vars, collapse = "\n")
res_swb <- paste0(swb_vars, " ~~ rw", times, "*", swb_vars, collapse = "\n")

# Residual covariance labels
res_cov <- paste0(outcome_vars, " ~~ rc", times, "*", swb_vars, collapse = "\n")

# Bivariate LGCM template
rq3_template_24m <- paste0('
# Define intercept and slope factors
ia =~ ', i_loadings_out, '
sa =~ ', s_loadings_out, '

iw =~ ', i_loadings_swb, '
sw =~ ', s_loadings_swb, '

# Regress latent growth factors on baseline age
ia ~ bia*age_base_z
sa ~ bsa*age_base_z
iw ~ biw*age_base_z
sw ~ bsw*age_base_z

# Mean structure
ia ~ a0*1
sa ~ a1*1
iw ~ w0*1
sw ~ w1*1

# Variance structure
ia ~~ via*ia
sa ~~ vsa*sa
ia ~~ cisa*sa

iw ~~ viw*iw
sw ~~ vsw*sw
iw ~~ cisw*sw

# Cross-process covariances
ia ~~ cii*iw
ia ~~ cis_aw*sw
iw ~~ cis_wa*sa
sa ~~ css*sw

# Residual variances
', res_out, '

', res_swb, '

# Residual covariances
', res_cov, '
')
```

#### Template loop & extraction

Run loop over all 5 X 2 outcomes  

(Here, I suppress lavaan warnings in the html output, but they are very similar to the ones shown above for the example model. Below, I go into model diagnostics more systematically.)  

```{r rq3-loop-24}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_models) { # we can toggle this on/off in the YAML heading
  
# Loop across all attachment outcomes
for (i in 1:length(outcomes$short)) {
  print(paste0("Running outcome: ", outcomes$maj[i]))

  # Fill bivariate LGCM template
  model_rq3_24m <- stringr::str_replace_all(rq3_template_24m, "outcome", outcomes$short[i])
  
  # Outcome-specific missingness indicator -> added this mostly for parent-specific attachment
  missi_var <- paste0(outcomes$short[i], "_missi")

  # Fit model in consistently single people
  fit_rq3_24m <- lavaan::growth(model_rq3_24m,
                                data = df_atta_wide_single_c %>% filter(.data[[missi_var]] == 0),
                                missing = "fiml",
                                verbose = FALSE)

  # Save model object
  eval(call("<-", as.name(paste0("fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m")), fit_rq3_24m))
  saveRDS(fit_rq3_24m, file = paste0("models/fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[i], "_24m.rds"))
}
}
```

Create summary table of all effects of interest: parameter extraction  

```{r rq3-load-extract-24}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Load saved models when run_models = FALSE
if (!params$run_models) {
  
  for (x in outcomes$short) {
    assign(paste0("fit_rq3_", x, "_24m"), readRDS(paste0("models/fit_rq3_", x, "_24m.rds")))
  }
}

# custom function for parameter extraction from bivariate LGCMs
# same function as above

# bind all model outputs together
rq3_summary_24m <- bind_rows(
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_glo_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_rom_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fri_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_mot_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_avoi_fat_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_glo_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_rom_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fri_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_mot_24m),
  extract_lav_rq3(fit_rq3_anxi_fat_24m)
)
# Add labels
rq3_summary_24m <- rq3_summary_24m %>% 
  mutate(outc = str_remove(outc, "_24m"),
         outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short,
                           labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE))
```

For the preregistered effects of interest, I use lavaan::standardizedSolution(). For the cross-construct latent growth-factor covariances, standardization yields correlations rather than covariances. The standardized estimates have their own SEs, CIs, and p-values, which can differ slightly from those of the corresponding unstandardized covariances. This matches the preregistration: “The main effects of interest are the cross-construct intercept-slope correlations and slope-slope correlations.”  

The standardized effect size is always the same as the est_std / std.all one from broom::tidy(), though.  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_models_24m <- c("fit_rq3_avoi_glo_24m", "fit_rq3_avoi_rom_24m",
                "fit_rq3_avoi_fri_24m", "fit_rq3_avoi_mot_24m",
                "fit_rq3_avoi_fat_24m", "fit_rq3_anxi_glo_24m",
                "fit_rq3_anxi_rom_24m", "fit_rq3_anxi_fri_24m",
                "fit_rq3_anxi_mot_24m", "fit_rq3_anxi_fat_24m")

# Extract all RQ3 slope-slope correlations
rq3_extracted_cross_24m <- bind_rows(lapply(rq3_models_24m, function(x) {
  extract_rq3_cross_std(get(x), x) %>% 
    mutate(outc = stringr::str_remove(outc, "_24m")) # added this here
})) %>% 
  mutate(outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(domain_fct = factor(str_remove(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety): "), 
                             levels = c("Global", "Romantic", "Best Friend", "Mother", "Father"),
                             ordered = TRUE),
         pred_fct = factor(str_extract(outc_fct, "^(Avoidance|Anxiety)"), 
                           levels = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety"),
                           ordered = TRUE)) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, term) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, domain_fct, pred_fct)
```

#### Model fit

Fit statistics:  
-> These fit indices are very computationally expensive. I put them in a conditional chunk and load them as an RDS object in the next chunk.  

```{r calc-fit-rq3-24m}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

if (params$run_expensive) { # only run when we allow this in YAML heading
  
# model fit statistics: single-group models
rq3_fit_single_24m <- outcomes$short %>% 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(x) {
    bind_rows(
      broom::glance(get(paste0("fit_rq3_", x, "_24m"))) %>% 
        mutate(outc = x, group_fct = "Consistently single"))
  }) %>% 
  select(outc, group_fct, nobs, npar, AIC, BIC, cfi, rmsea, srmr) %>% 
  mutate(
    outc_fct = factor(outc, levels = outcomes$short, labels = outcomes$maj, ordered = TRUE),
    group_fct = factor(group_fct,
                       levels = c("Consistently single",
                                  "Consistently partnered",
                                  "Intermittently partnered"),
                       ordered = TRUE))

# save externally:
saveRDS(rq3_fit_single_24m, "model_fit/rq3_fit_single_24m.rds")
}
```

Show fit indices table: 
```{r show-fit-rq3-24m}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false

rq3_fit_single_24m <- readRDS("model_fit/rq3_fit_single_24m.rds")

rq3_fit_single_24m %>% select(-outc) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, everything()) %>% 
  kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Again, somewhat better fit here compared to the 30-months model.  
:::

#### Model diagnostics

- Did the model converge?  
- Did lavaan's internal check pass?  
- Are there inadmissible negative variances?  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# diagnostics for all single-group and partnered RQ2 models
rq3_diagnostics_24m <- purrr::map_dfr(rq3_models_24m, function(x) {
  fit <- get(x)
  tibble(
    model = x,
    converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    post_check = lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
    neg_variances = any(parameterEstimates(fit)$op == "~~" &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$lhs == parameterEstimates(fit)$rhs &
                          parameterEstimates(fit)$est < 0))
})

rq3_diagnostics_24m %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
All good.  
:::

#### Summary tables

Latent intercept and slope factors: "alpha0" (a0 = attach, w0 = life sat) & "alpha1" (a1 = attach, w1 = life sat): 

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_24m_a <- rq3_summary_24m %>% 
  filter(term=="a0" | term=="a1" | term=="w0" | term=="w1") %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, group_fct, term) %>% 
  mutate(sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, sig, est_std)

rq3_table_24m_a %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 4, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_24m_a))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Very similar to the 30-months model. This one estimates slightly less life satisfaction increases and less attachment changes (mostly decreases), which is roughly proportional to the shortening of the time window. 
:::

Latent intercept / slope variances & covariance - general terminology:  
- (a) = attachment  
- (w) = well-being (life satisf.)  
- (c) = covariance (or: correlation in the standardized solution)  
- (v) = variance  
- (i) = latent intercept  
- (s) = latent slope   

Cross-construct correlations (which correspond to the hypotheses):  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_24m_cross <- rq3_extracted_cross_24m %>% 
  filter(term %in% c("cii", "cis_aw", "cis_wa", "css")) %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, term) %>% 
  mutate(group = "Consistently single", 
         sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, sig)

rq3_table_24m_cross %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 4, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_24m_cross))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Super similar intercept-intercept correlations (to the 30-m. model).  

Also relatively similar intercept-slope correlations. (Here and there, an association slips above p < .05 threshold but no major differences in effect sizes).  
:::

Focus on parameter that is relevant to hypothesis: slope-slope correlation (standardized solution)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_24m_cross %>% 
  filter(term=="css") %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Again, very similar correlations (to the 30-m. model).  
:::

Within-construct intercept-slope covariances:  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_24m_cis <- rq3_summary_24m %>% 
  filter(term %in% c("cisa", "cisw")) %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, group_fct) %>% 
  mutate(sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_value, sig, est_std)

rq3_table_24m_cis %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 2, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_24m_cis))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Very similar!
:::

Variances of the latent intercept and slope factors: (via, viw) & (vis, vws)  

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

rq3_table_24m_v <- rq3_summary_24m %>% 
  filter(stringr::str_starts(term, "v")) %>% 
  arrange(outc_fct, group_fct, term) %>% 
  mutate(sig = case_when(p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**", p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")) %>% 
  select(outc_fct, group_fct, term, est, ci_lo, ci_hi)

rq3_table_24m_v %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format = "html") %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("bordered")) %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 4, length.out = nrow(rq3_table_24m_v))),
                       background = "lightgrey")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Overall, pretty similar but some differences in the slope variances.
:::

#### Summary plot

We're plotting the standardized effects (i.e., slope-slope correlations).  

Create and save plot:  
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: false
#| cache: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Plot standardized slope-slope correlations
plot_rq3_css_24m <- ggplot(rq3_extracted_cross_24m %>% filter(term=="css"), 
                           aes(x = est, y = forcats::fct_rev(domain_fct),
                               colour = forcats::fct_rev(pred_fct), 
                               shape = forcats::fct_rev(pred_fct))) +
  geom_rect(data = bg_df_rq3,
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = NULL),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = bg_df_rq3$fill,
            alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi), 
                 height = 0.3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6),
                 linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Avoidance" = "#D55E00", "Anxiety" = "#0072B2"),
                      breaks = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Avoidance" = 17, "Anxiety" = 16),
                     breaks = c("Avoidance", "Anxiety")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.60, 0.20), 
                     breaks = seq(-0.60, 0.20, by = 0.20),
                     labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
                     oob = scales::oob_keep) +
  labs(x = "Slope-slope correlation (95% CI)", 
       y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3), panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Attachment variable"),
         shape = guide_legend(title = "Attachment variable"))

# save as pdf
pdf(width = 6, height = 4.5, "figures/rq3_plot_css_24m.pdf")
plot_rq3_css_24m
dev.off()
```

Show plot: 
```{r rq3-summary-plot-24m-show}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| cache: false

plot_rq3_css_24m
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Nothing changes in terms of significance evaluation (compared to the 30-m. model). Slightly smaller correlation for romantic avoidance, though. 
:::

#### Full model results

##### `r outcomes$maj[1]`

Full model results for `r outcomes$min[1]` (in the consistently single people):

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| output: true
#| cache: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

broom::tidy(get(paste0("fit_rq3_", outcomes$short[1], "_24m")), conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>% 
  filter(label != "") %>% 
  arrange(label) %>% 
  select(term = label, est = estimate, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high, p_value = p.value, est_std = std.all) %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
